Characteristic: A Certain Brāhmaṇa told the Kurusabhā (8. 30. 8) that the people of Pañcanada did not follow the ancient धर्म (धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति सन्तो मद्रान् ऋते पञ्चनदांश् च … ) 8. 30. 62; having seen the धर्म practised by the people of Pañcanada, Prajāpati exclaimed ‘fie’!; it was thus censured by Prajāpati (धर्मं पाञ्चनदं दृष्ट्वा धिग् इत्य् आह प्रजापतिः ।  … इति पाञ्चनदं धर्मम् अवमेने पिता-महः) 8. 30. 65-66; the पाञ्चनद धर्म is characterized as ingratitude, looting wealth belonging to others, drinking wine, violating the wife of a teacher; for them there was no अधर्म (कृतघ्नता पर-वित्तापहारः सुरापानं गुरुदारावमर्-शः । येषां धर्मस् तान् प्रति नास्त्य् अधर्-मः) 8. 30. 74; their country was very large, full of riches and corn (एष देशः सुविस्तीर्णः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्) 5. 19. 31; prosperous, very prosperous (स्फीत) 14. 84. 17; (अतिसमृद्धिमन्त्) 16. 8. 43. D. Epic events: (1) The Pañca-nada country was subjugated by Nakula in his expedition to the west of Indra-prastha (प्रतीचीम् नकुलो राजन् दिशं व्यजयत् 2. 23. 10; वासुदेवजिताम् आशां … व्यजयत् 2. 29. 1) before the Rājasūya 2. 29. 10; (2) The large army of the Kaura-vas spread out as far as Pañcanada and other countries near Hāstinapura 5. 19. 29; (3) Before the war, when the Kaurava army got ready, Bhīṣma stood at the head of it along with Pañcanada and other warriors 6. 20. 10; (4) On the third day of the war, Pañcanadas were posted at the ‘neck’ of the Gāruḍavyūha (6. 52. 2) of the Kauravas 6. 52. 5; (5) The Aśva-medha horse reached Pañcanada from the western ocean and from Pañcanada it went to Gāndhāra country (पश्चिमं देशं समुद्रस्य तदा हयः । … व्यचरत् … ततः पञ्चनदं ययौ ॥ तस्माद् अपि स कौरव्य गान्धारविषयं हयः । विचचार) 14. 84. 17-18; (6) While Arjuna was on his way from Dvārakā to Hāstinapura, he arrived at Pañcanada and stayed there; he was attacked by the Ābhīras (Dasyus 16. 8. 44) who lived in Pañcanada and kidnapped the Vṛṣṇi women in his charge 16. 8. 43-61; (आभीरैर्॥।हृताः पञ्चनदा-लयैः) 16. 9. 16 [for Pañcanada also see Vol. I. 379].
पञ्च: Pañca nadyaḥ f. (pl.): Five rivers, not specified. Duryodhana assures Yudhiṣṭhira during the game of dice that if the Pāṇḍavas successfully passed the thirteenth year un-known to the spies of the Kauravas, the latter would get back the five rivers (तवैव ता भारत पञ्चनद्यः) (i. e. the kingdom of the region marked by the five rivers) 3. 35. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 34. 11. वितस्तादि-पञ्चनद्युपलक्षितो देशः); the five rivers, excluding the Sindhu, are counted by Mārka-ṇḍeya among those that are described as mothers of the fire-hearths (i. e. sacrifices were offered on their banks (for Nī. see Kapilā) (सिन्धुवर्जं पञ्च नद्यो … एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्-तिताः) 3. 212. 21, 24. [See Pañcanada above and Pañcanada in Section 1. 5 A]
पञ्चयज्ञा: Pañcayajñā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting the तीर्थ (अभिगम्य) one is glorified in the heaven 3. 82. 9.
पञ्चवट: Pañcavaṭa m.: Name of a sacred place. One who has observed chastity and has controlled his senses (ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्-रियः), if he visits the Pañcavaṭa he secures great merit and is glorified in the world of the righteous (पुण्येन महता युक्तः सतां लोके महीयते); God Sthāṇu (Śiva) himself is present there; just by visiting the place and by worshipping god Śiva one gets success (तम् अर्चयित्वा देवेशं गमनाद् एव सिध्यति) 3. 81. 141-142.
पञ्चस्रोतस्: Pañcasrotas nt.: Name of a place marked by five streams ? (identical with Pañcanada ?) Pañcaśikha, the first pupil of Āsuri, was once engaged in a long sacrificial session lasting for a thousand years at Pañcasrotas (पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रम् आस्ते वर्षस-हस्रिकम्) 12. 211. 10 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 218. 10: पञ्च स्रोतांसि विषयकेदारप्रणालिका यस्य तस्मिन् मनसि मानसं सत्रम् इत्य् अर्थः). [See Pañca-nada, Pañca nadyaḥ]

Pañcasrotas nt.: Name of a place (?) The great sage Pañcaśikha, who was looked upon as Kapila incarnate (12. 211. 9), the first pupil of Āsuri, had performed a सत्र, lastīng for a thousand years, at Pañcasrotas (पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रम् आस्ते वर्षसहस्रिकम्) 12. 211. 10 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 218. 10: पञ्च स्रोतांसि विषयकेदारप्रणालिका यस्य तस्मिन् मनसि मानसं सत्रम् इत्य् अर्थः).
पद्मसरस्: Padmasaras nt.: Name of a lake. Described as pleasing (रम्य); Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna, starting for the Magadha from the land of the Kurus and passing through Kurujāṅgala, first reached Padma-saras before crossing the Kālakūṭa mountain 2. 18. 26.
पम्पा: Pampā f.: Name of a large lake (तटाकिनी 3. 263. 40). A. Location: Located near the mountain Ṛśyamūka 3. 263. 40. B. Description: Its water was auspicious (शिवजला) 3. 263. 40; frequented by swans and ducks (हंस-कारण्डवायुता) 3. 263. 40; a lotus pond having many day blooming and night-bloom-ing lotuses in it (नलिनीं प्रभूतकमलोत्-पलाम्) 3. 264. 1; a very cool and pleasing breeze, having the fragrance of nectar, blows in the forest near the Pampā (मारुतेन सुशीतेन सुखेनामृतगन्धिना । सेव्यमानो वने तस्मिन्) 3. 264. 2. C. Rāmāyaṇa events: Sugrīva and his four counsellors lived near the Pampā 3. 263. 41; Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa reached the lake in order to meet Sugrīva 3. 264. 1; they drank its water and gave offerings to manes before proceeding towards Ṛśyamūka (तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् अपि) 3. 264. 8-9.
पयोष्णी: Payoṣṇī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed twice by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 15, 19; in the south 3. 86. 1; near the Vindhya mountain (एष विन्ध्यो महाशैलः पयोष्णी च समुद्रगा) 3. 58. 21; one could proceed from there to the mountain Vai-ḍūrya and the Narmadā (स पयोष्ण्यां  … स्नात्वा … वैडूर्यपर्वतं चैव नर्-मदां च … समाजगाम) 3. 121. 15. B. Description: Very holy (महापुण्या) 3. 83. 37; having excellent तीर्थस् on it (सुतीर्था) 3. 120. 30; having pleasant तीर्थस् on it (रम्यतीर्था), having ample water (बहुजला), and visited by the Brāhmaṇas (द्विजसेविता) 3. 86. 4; excellent river (सरि-तां वरा) 3. 83. 37; flowing to the ocean (समुद्रगा) 3. 58. 21; made prosperous (?) by the king of Vidarbha (विदर्भ-राजोपचिता) 3. 120. 30; river of king Nṛga (सरिन् णृगस्य) 3. 86. 4; its water is mixed with the Soma pressed (on its bank) (सुतेन सोमेन विमिश्रितोदा) 3. 120. 30; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Epic event: Yudhiṣṭhira, while on pilgrimage, reached the river Payoṣṇī and lived there 3. 120. 30; Dhaumya advised the Pāṇḍavas to bathe in the river and be freed from sins 3. 121. 14; accordingly they bathed and proceed-ed towards the Vaiḍūrya mountain and the river Narmadā 3. 121. 15. D. Past events: (1) On the river Payoṣṇī gods with Indra, and the Prajāpatis, offered many kinds of sacrifices giving large दक्षिणास् 3. 121. 2; (2) On its bank king Nṛga gave satisfaction to Indra with Soma and gave ample दक्षिणास् 3. 121. 1; 3. 86. 6; here the great ascetic Mārkaṇḍeya sang a गाथा in the presence of king Nṛga, describing his genealogy, at the time of his sacrifice (अनुवंश्यां जगौ गाथां नृगस्य धरणीपतेः ॥ नृगस्य यजमानस्य प्रत्यक्षम् इति नः श्रुतम् । ) 3. 86. 5-6 (Nī. on 3. 88. 5; अनुवंश्यां वंशानुरूपां न तु मृग-(? नृग) मात्रानुरूपाम्); (3) Here king Gaya, the son of Amūrtarayas, satisfied Indra with Soma in his seven horse sacrifices 3. 121. 3. E. Holiness: (1) There were many आश्रमस् of great sages on the river 3. 58. 21; (2) By worshipping manes and gods on the Payoṣṇī one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 37; (3) One who bathes (उपस्पृश्य) in the Payoṣṇī is freed of sins (धूतपाप्मा भविष्यसि) 3. 121. 14; (4) If one were to bathe (उपस्पृशेत्) in the river Payoṣṇī he would obtain the world obtained by Gaya (i. e. the world of Indra) 3. 121. 13.
परा: Parā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the uni-verse and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
पर्णाशा: Parṇāśā f.: Name of a river. (1) Described as a great river (माहा-नदी) 7. 67. 44; excellent river (सरितां वरा) 7. 67. 47; having cool water (शीततोया) 7. 67. 44; (2) She was the mother of Śrutāyudha 7. 67. 44, 57; the river gave birth to this son from Varuṇa; she wanted a son who could not be killed by his enemies (अवध्यो ऽयं भवेल् लोके शत्रूणां तनयो मम) 7. 67. 44-45; Varuṇa, however, gave the son a heavenly missile and made him unassailable by enemies as he could not make a mortal immortal (नास्ति चाप्य् अमर-त्वं वै मनुष्यस्य कथंचन । … दुर्धर्षस् त्व् एष शत्रूणां रणेषु भविता सदा) 7. 67. 47-48; (3) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16, 2. [See Pūrṇāśā]
पलाशक: Palāśaka m. pl.: Name of a holy place. Situated in the north 3. 88. 1; described as holy (पुण्येषु) and pleasing (रम्येषु) 3. 88. 13; Jamadagni offered a sacrifice at the Palāśakas (जमदग्निर् महायशाः । पलाश-केषु … अयजताभिभूः) 3. 88. 13; at this sacrifice all the excellent rivers brought their water and waited on Jamadagni; a श्लोक to this effect was sung here by Viśvāvasu himself 3. 88. 14-16.
पलाशिनी: Palāśinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
पवनस्य: Pavanasya hradaḥ m.: Name of a lake sacred to the Maruts. Described as an excellent तीर्थ of the Maruts (मरुतां तीर्थम् उत्तमम्) 3. 81. 88; by bathing in this तीर्थ one is glorified in the world of Vāyu (वायुलोके महीयते) 3. 81. 88.
पवित्रा: Pavitrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पाका: Pākā f.: Name of a river. Mentioned among those rivers by visiting which one becomes auspicious, assumes a heavenly form and, wearing heavenly garlands and full of holy fragrance, reaches the Goloka (? गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 47-48 (for citation see Karatoyinī).
पाणिखात: Pāṇikhāta nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing here and by giving offerings to gods (तर्पयित्वा च देवताः) one gets the fruit of a Rājasūya and goes to the world of sages (ऋषिलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 81. 75.
पापहरा: Pāpaharā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पारा: Pārā f.: Name of a river. [See Kauśikī]
पारिप्लव: Pāriplava nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत); by visiting this तीर्थ one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra 3. 81. 10.
पारिषेणा: Pāriṣeṇā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13; (for other details see Palāśinī).
पिङ्गा: Piṅgā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the Arbuda mountain (?) 3. 80. 74; one who has observed chastity and has controlled his senses (ब्रह्मचारि जितेन्द्रियः) if he bathes there (उपस्पृश्य) he gets the reward of gifting a hundred कपिला cows 3. 80. 76.
पिच्छिला: Picchilā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 28, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पिञ्जला: Piñjalā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13 (for other details see Palaśinī).
पितामहसरस्: Pitāmahasaras nt.: Name of a holy lake. Situated on the Śailarāja (i. e. Hima-vant ?) (शैलराजप्रतिष्ठितम्) 3. 82. 128; from this lake rises the river Kumāradhārā 3. 82. 129, and also the river Sarasvatī 9. 41. 29; by bathing in this lake (तत्रा-भिषेकं कुर्वाणः) one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 82. 128. [See Puṣkara]
पितामहस्य: Pitāmahasya uttaravedi f.: See Prajā-pateḥ vedī2.
पिप्पलावती: Pippalāvatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पुण्य: Puṇya nt.: Name of a sacred lake. Situated near the river Pārā (i. e. the river Kauśikī) and the mountains Maināka and Asita 3. 87. 9, 7; Lomaśa advised Yudhi-ṣṭhira to bathe silently in the lake (तूष्णीं … समुपस्पृश) 3. 135. 7.

Puṇya m.: Name (?) of an आश्रम। The आश्रम of the high-souled Kāśyapa on the river Kauśikī was called Puṇya (आश्रमश् चैव पुण्याख्यः काश्यपस्य महात्मनः) 3. 110. 2 [See Kāśyapāśrama; for Puṇya, name of a तीर्थ, see Vol. 1. 383].
पुरमालिनी: Puramālinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पुरापवर्तन: Purāpavartana nt.: Name of a sacred place. By repairing to (सेव्य) Purāpavartana, one who is controlled (दान्तः) and causes no injury to others (अहिंसकः) is served in the Nandana forest by the Apsarases 13. 26. 42.
पुरु: Puru m.: Name of a mountain. Where Purūravas was born (पर्वतश् च पुरुर् नाम यत्र जातः पुरूरवाः) 3. 88. 19.
पुरुही: Puruhī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
पुष्करारण्य: Puṣkarāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest where there is the तीर्थ Puṣkara. A. Location: In the west (2. 29. 2). B. Epic events: (1) Nakula, in his ex-pedition to the west before the Rājasūya, con-quered the Gaṇas called the Utsavasaṃketas who lived in the Puṣkarāraṇya 2. 29. 7-8; (2) Takṣaka, when he came to know the curse of Kadrū, started practising severe austerities at various sacred places one of them being the Puṣkarāraṇya 1. 32. 3. C. Holy: If one resorts to the Puṣkarāraṇya and feeds only a single Brāhmaṇa he rejoices as a result of that act in this and the next world (प्रेत्य चेह च मोदते); and, if he gives there to a Brāhmaṇa, faithfully and without malice (श्रद्धावान् अनसूयकः), vegetables, roots and fruits on which he himself subsists, then by that act, he gets the fruit of a horse sacri-fice 3. 80. 49-50.
पुष्पन्यास: Puṣpanyāsa m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing at the Puṣpanyāsa one does not grieve over death (उपस्पृश्य न शोचेन् मरणं ततः) 3. 80. 114.
पुष्पवती: Puṣpavatī f.: Name of a sacred bathing place. By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) at the Puṣpa-vatī and by fasting there for three nights one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows and lifts up his family 3. 83. 12.
पुष्पवत्: Puṣpavant m.: Name of a mountain in the Kuśadvīpa. The fourth of the six mountains in the Kuśadvīpa 6. 13. 10; all these mountains are described as the best among the mountains (पर्वतोत्तमाः) 6. 13. 11; the distance between these six mountains doubles as one moves from the one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 13. 11.
पुष्पवन्त्: Puṣpavant m.: Name of a mountain in the Kuśadvīpa. The fourth of the six mountains in the Kuśadvīpa 6. 13. 10; all these mountains are described as the best among the mountains (पर्वतोत्तमाः) 6. 13. 11; the distance between these six mountains doubles as one moves from the one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 13. 11.
पुष्पवेणी: Puṣpaveṇī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 33, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
पूर्णाशा: Pūrṇāśā f.: Name of a river. Described as a great river (महानदी); listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13; (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī). [Identical with Parṇāśā ?]
पूर्वान्तगण्डिका: Pūrvāntagaṇḍikā f.: Name of a range of hills (?) It lies on the eastern peak of the Mālya-vant mountain (in the Uttara Kurus) (तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे पूर्वे पूर्वान्तगण्डिका) 6. 8. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 7. 28: गण्डिका क्षुद्रपर्वतः).
पूर्वाभिरामा: Pūrvābhirāmā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13; (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
पृथिव्यास्: Pṛthivyās tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting the Pṛthivītīrtha (पृथिव्यास् तीर्थम् आसाद्य) one secures the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 11.
पृथूदक: Pṛthūdaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the northern bank of the Sarasvatī (तीर्थम् … सरस्वत्याः; सर-स्वत्युत्तरे तीरे) 9. 38. 25-27, 29; 12. 148. 10. B. Description: Famous, famous in the three worlds (ख्यात, त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत) 3. 81. 122; holy (पुण्य) 12. 148. 10; ritually pure, clean and sanctifying (मेध्य, पवित्र, पावन) 3. 81. 128; the best of all the तीर्थस् (उत्तमे सर्वतीर्थानाम्) 3. 81. 126; the holiest of all (पृथूदकात् पुण्य-तमं नान्यत् तीर्थम्) 3. 81. 128, 125. C. Presiding deity: Sacred to Kārtikeya 3. 81. 122. D. Holiness: (1) One should bathe at the Pṛthūdaka (अभिषेकं कुर्वीत) and be engaged in worship of manes and gods; just a bath there (स्नातमात्रस्य) destroys whatever inauspicious deed (अशुभं कर्म) a man or a woman does, either knowingly or unknowingly as a human being (अज्ञानाज् ज्ञनतो वापि … कृतं मानुष-बुद्धिना); it secures for him the fruit of an Aśvamedha and leads him to heaven 3. 81. 122-124; the wise say that even sinners go to heaven by bathing at the Pṛthūdaka 3. 81. 129; (2) One who gives up his body at the Pṛthūdaka while muttering prayers is not affected by the fear of imminent death (यस् त्यजेद् आत्मनस् तनुम् ॥ पृथूदके जप्यपरो नैनं श्वोमरणं तपेत्) 3. 81. 126; 9. 38. 29; in a Gāthā sung by Yayāti it is said that one who bathes in or drinks water of the Pṛthūdaka is not affected by imminent death (यत्रावगाह्य पीत्वा वा नैव श्वोमरणं तपेत्) 12. 148. 10; (3) Sanatkumāra and Vyāsa have sung (a Gāthā ?) which says that a visit to the Pṛthūdaka is prescribed in the Veda (वेदे च नियतं) 3. 81. 127; (4) The Pṛthūdaka is holier than even the Kurukṣetra, the Sarasvatī, and all the other तीर्थस् 3. 81. 125. E. Epic event: Balarāma visited this place and after bathing there (आप्लुत्य  … उपस्पृश्य) gave many gifts to the Brāh-maṇas 9. 38. 23, 30. F. Past event: Ruṣaṅgu, a Brāhmaṇa ascetic, decided in oldage to give up his body and told his sons to take him to the Pṛthūdaka; his sons took him there where he was given bath according to the prescribed rites (विधिना … आप्लुतः); Ruṣaṅgu gave up his body there 9. 38. 24-28, 23.
प्रजापतेर्: Prajāpater uttaravedi f.: See Prajā-pateḥ vedī2.
प्रजापतेः: Prajāpateḥ vedī1 f.: Designation of a sacred place. A. Formation: Prayāga, Pratiṣṭhāna, Kambala, Aśvatara and the Bhogavatī तीर्थ constitute the Vedī of Prajāpati (वेदी प्रोक्ता प्रजापतेः) 3. 83. 72; (3. 93. 7); described as frequented by ascetics (तपस्विजनजुष्टा) 3. 93. 7. B. Holiness: There the Vedas and the sacrifices in bodily form, as well as the sages observing important vows, wait upon Prajāpati; gods and Cakracaras offer sacrifices there 3. 83. 72-73 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 72: चक्रचराः सूर्यादयः). C. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas, in their तीर्थयात्रा, visited it in the company of Brāhmaṇas; living there they practised the best austerities and constantly satisfied the Brāhmaṇas by giving them offerings obtained in the forest (वन्येन हविषा) 3. 93. 7-8. [See Prajāpateḥ vedī2]

Prajāpateḥ vedī2 f.: Designation of a sacred place. The land of the high-souled Kuru, i. e. the Kurukṣetra, along the river Sarasvatī, is known as the Vedī of Prajāpati; it is five योजनस् in extent all around (वेदी प्रजा-पतेर् एषा समन्तात् पञ्चयोजना) 3. 129. 22; listed among the places which form the boundary of the Kurukṣetrasamantapañcaka where the name occurs as Prajāpater uttara-vedi 9. 52. 20; (Pitāmahasya uttaravedi) 3. 81. 178; here the divine sages, as also the royal sages and sages offered sacrifices with the help of Brāhmaṇas related to the river Sarasvatī (इह सारस्वतैर् यज्ञैर् इष्ट-वन्तः सुरर्षयः । ऋषयश् चैव कौन्तेय तथा राजर्षयो ऽपि च ॥ ) 3. 129. 20-21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 14: सारस्वतैः ब्राह्मणैः). [See Prajāpateḥ vedī1, Pla-kṣāvataraṇa]
प्रतिष्ठान: Pratiṣṭhāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the five तीर्थस् which together form the Vedī of Prajāpati 3. 83. 72; there the Vedas and the sacrifices, in bodily form, and the sages observing great vows wait upon Prajāpati; gods and Cakracaras offer sacri-fies there 3. 83. 73. [See Prajāpateḥ vedī1]

Pratiṣṭhāna nt.: Name of a city. Suparṇa took Gālava to king Yayāti in Pratiṣṭhāna to ask him if he could pro-vide Gālava with eight hundred white horses with one black ear each 5. 112. 9. [For Pratiṣṭhāna, a तीर्थ, see Vol. 1. 388]
प्रभास: Prabhāsa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ; its original name Hiraṇyasaras (12. 329. 46(5)). A. Location: In the Surāṣṭras (सु-राष्ट्रेषु) 3. 86. 16; on the western ocean (पश्चिमस्यां दिशि समुद्रे) 12. 329. 46; (उदधौ) 3. 86. 17; (समुद्रे पश्चिमे) 1. 210. 2, 1; 13. 96. 3; (समुद्रान्ते) 16. 4. 10; (तीर्थं महोदधेः) 3. 119. 3; a तीर्थ on the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्या वरे तीर्थे) 9. 34. 67; (तीर्थं सरस्वत्याः) 9. 34. 69. B. Etymology: Its original name was Hiraṇyasaras; after the moon (Soma) bathed there and was freed of sin, he became bright; the तीर्थ then came to be known as Prabhāsa (तत्र चावभासितस् तीर्थे यदा सोमस् तदाप्रभृति तीर्थं तत् प्रभासम् इति नाम्ना ख्यातं बभूव) 12. 329. 46 (10); (प्रभासनात् तस्य ततः प्रभासः) 9. 34. 37; 9. 34. 76-77; (एतत् प्रभासते तीर्थम्) 3. 130. 7. C. Des-cription: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 119. 1; 3. 130. 7; 9. 34. 36; (3. 86. 16); suitable for holy people (पुण्यजनोचित) 3. 13. 14; purifying (पवित्र) 3. 130. 7; destroying sins (पाप-नाशन) 3. 130. 7; excellent (वर) 9. 34. 67; (तीर्थवर) 3. 80. 78; (तीर्थप्रवर) 9. 34. 37, 38; (तीर्थानां प्रवरम्) 9. 34. 75; great, best (परम) 9. 34. 69; (उत्तम) 9. 34. 76; famous on the earth, famous in the worlds (पृथिव्यां प्रथितम्) 3. 118. 15; (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 80. 77; the तीर्थ of the gods (त्रिदशानां तीर्थम्) 3. 86. 17; dear to Indra (इन्द्रस्य दयितम्) 3. 130. 7. D. Epic events: (1) During his exile Arjuna, after visiting the other तीर्थस् on the west coast, went to Prabhāsa; Kṛṣṇa, hav-ing come to know that Arjuna had arrived at the Prabhāsadeśa, went there to meet him; the two met at Prabhāsa; they sported there according to their wishes and from there they went to the Raivataka mountain 1. 210. 2-4, 8; (2) The Brāhmaṇas wished to visit the Prabhāsa and the other तीर्थस् along with Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 91. 10; (3) After visiting Śūrpāraka, Yudhiṣṭhira went to Prabhāsa; he bathed there and, with his brothers and Kṛṣṇā, gave offerings to gods and manes; the Brāhmaṇas and Lomaśa too offered there to gods and manes; Yudhiṣṭhira practised there severe austerities 3. 118. 15-17; (4) Balarāma and Janārdana, along with the Vṛṣṇi heroes, went to Prabhāsa to meet the Pāṇḍavas; the Pāṇḍavas and the Vṛṣṇis held consultations together at Prabhāsa 3. 118. 18; 3. 119. 1-3; (5) Arjuna, in his wander-ings with the sacrificial horse, came to Prabhāsa from Gokarṇa 14. 84. 12; (6) Balarāma, in his तीर्थयात्रा, first went to Prabhāsa 9. 34. 36; (7) The Yādavas, desirous of visiting a तीर्थ, went to Prabhāsa and lived there; there they were engaged in a drinking bout (प्रावर्तत महापानं प्रभासे); in the mutual kill-ing that followed the Vṛṣṇi heroes, the Bhojas and the Andhakas were all destroyed at Prabhāsa 16. 9. 8-9. E. Past and my-thological events: (1) At Prabhāsa Kṛṣṇa, observing restraint (नियमे स्थितः) stood on one foot for a thousand divine years (दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम्) to practise aus-terities 3. 13. 14; (2) The sages Śukra, Aṅgiras and others who came together at Prabhāsa thought of going on a तीर्थयात्रा from there; (3) Soma was cursed by Dakṣa; as a result he was emaciated and could not shine; Dakṣa Prajāpati advised him to go to the तीर्थ of Sarasvatī (i. e. Prabhāsa) and emerge from there after taking a bath; when Soma did this he could wax again; but for one half of the month he would wane; so Soma went to Prabhāsa and emerged after bath on the new moon day; he could illuminate the worlds; the gods then reached Prabhāsa and, in the company of Soma, met Dakṣa; this is why Prabhāsa became the most excellent of all the तीर्थस् (प्र-भासं च यथा तीर्थं तीर्थानां प्र-वरं ह्य् अभूत्); on every new moon day the moon bathes in Prabhāsa and waxes again; that is why Prabhāsa is so called 9. 34. 67-77; 9. 34. 36-39; (the bath in the Hiraṇyasaras तीर्थ, which later became known as Prabhāsa, was prescribed for Soma by the sages 12. 329. 46). F. Holiness: (1) If one who is pure and has a controll-ed mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः) bathes at Prabhāsa he secures for himself the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra sacrifice 3. 80. 78; (2) According to Aṅgiras one who bathes in Prabhāsa is awakened in a विमान by the praises of Apsarases 13. 26. 9; (3) According to Aṅgiras, again, one who with concentrated mind (समाहितः) spends one night of the new moon day (अमावास्याम्) at Prabhāsa has (as though) a second birth as a Siddha (सिद्ध्यते ऽत्र महाबाहो यो नरो जायते पुनः) 13. 26. 51; (4) According to a Gāthā sung by Yayāti one who visits Prabhāsa lives long again in this life (लब्धायुर् जीविते पुनः) 12. 148. 11; (5) If the high-souled persons, observing vows, visit Prabhāsa they become auspicious, obtain divine forms, wear divine garlands, and full of divine fragrance they reach the world of cows (? गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 45, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī). G. Importance: (1) God Agni himself is always present there (यत्र संनिहितो नित्यं स्वयम् एव हुताशनः) 3. 80. 77; (2) Men-tioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 18, 2.
प्रमाण: Pramāṇa m.: Name of a banyan tree. The Pāṇḍavas left Hāstinapura for their stay in the forest and started towards the north (उदङ्मुखाः) 3. 1. 9; at the end of the day they reached a big banyan tree (महावट), called Pramāṇa, on the bank of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā); they spent there that night partaking only of water (उदकेनैव तां रात्रिम् ऊषुस् ते) 3. 1. 39-40.
प्रयाग: Prayāga nt., m. (3. 83. 74): Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā (गङ्गायमुनयोर् वीर संगमम् … प्रयागम् इति विख्यातम्) 3. 85. 13-14; 3. 83. 70, 76, 80. B. Name explained: Prayāga (प्र-याग) so called because Pitāmaha (Prajāpati) in the bygone days offered a sacrifice there (यत्रायजत भूतात्मा पूर्वम् एव पितामहः । प्रया-गम् इति विख्यातं तस्माद् भरतसत्तम) 3. 85. 14. C. Description: Holy, most holy (पुण्य) 3. 85. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 87. 18: पुण्यं धर्मवृद्धिहेतुः); (पुण्यतम) 3. 83. 74; purifying (पवित्र) 3. 85. 13 (however, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 87. 17: पविः वज्रं तत्तुल्यं जन्ममरणादि-दुःखं तस्मात् त्रायत इति पवित्रम्); best sanctifier (पावनं उत्तमम्) 3. 85. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 87. 18: पावनं पापनाशनम्); famous, famous in the worlds (विख्यात) 3. 85. 14; (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 85. 13; liked by sages (ऋषिभिर् जुष्टम्) 3. 85. 13; praised by sages (ऋषिसंस्तुत) 3. 83. 65; place for sacrifices, honoured even by gods (यजनभूमिर् हि देवानाम् अपि सत्कृता) 3. 83. 77; place where gods offered sacrifice (देवयजन) 3. 93. 5; 5. 187. 26. D. Holiness: (1) No place is holier than Prayāga in the three worlds; Prayāga sur-passes by far all the other तीर्थस् (ततः पुण्यतमं नास्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत । प्रयागः सर्वतीर्थेभ्यः प्रभवत्य् अधि-कं विभो) 3. 83. 74 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 76: तथा च पृथिव्या अपत्यभूतानि तीर्थानि तत्फलभूताः स्वर्गाश् च तानि सर्वाणि प्रयागाद् उत्पन्नानीति प्रयागस्य तीर्थ-राजत्वम् उक्तम्); one is freed of sins either by hearing the name of the तीर्थ (श्रवणात्), or by reciting its name (नामसंकीर्तनाद् अपि), or by touching the earth there (मृत्ति-कालम्भनाद् वापि) 3. 83. 75; (2) If one who is strict in his vows (संशितव्रतः) and bathes at the confluence (of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā) at this तीर्थ, he gets the religious merit of performing a Rājasūya and an Aśvamedha 3. 83. 76; (3) If one who is controlled and strict in his vows (नियतः संशितव्रतः) bathes at Pra-yāga in the month of Māgha he becomes sinless (निर्मलः) and goes to heaven; (4) By just bathing (स्नात एव) at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā (at Prayāga) one acquires the religious merit that is obtained by one who has studied the four Vedas and by those who speak truth (चातुर्वेदे च यत् पुण्यं सत्यवादिषु चैव यत्) 3. 83. 80; (5) If one gives even a little there that assumes importance (तत्र दत्तं सूक्ष्मम् अपि महद् भवति भारत) 3. 83. 77; (6) Pulastya told Bhīṣma that if he decided to die at Prayāga he should not change his mind even at the instance of the Vedas or due to the advice of the people (न वेदवचनात् तात न लोकव-चनाद् अपि । मतिर् उत्क्रमणीया ते प्रयाग-मरणं प्रति) 3. 83. 78; (also see the next section). E. Importance: (1) At Prayāga are present Brahman and other gods, the quarters together with their rulers (दिशश् च सदिगीश्वराः), the Lokapālas, the Sādhyas, the Nairṛtas, manes, Sanatkumāra and other great sages (सनत्कुमारप्रमु-खास् तथैव परमर्षयः), Aṅgiras and other Brahmanical sages (अङ्गिरःप्रमुखाश् चैव तथा ब्रह्मर्षयः), the Nāgas, the Suparṇas, Siddhas, Cakracaras, rivers, oceans, the Gandharvas and the Apsa-rases, and god Hari followed by Prajāpati (हरिश् च भगवान् आस्ते प्रजाप्तिपुरस्-कृतः) 3. 83. 65-68 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 72: चक्रचराः सूर्यादयः); (2) Prayāga, Pratiṣṭhāna, Kambala, Aśvatara, and Bhogavatī together are known as the Vedī of Prajāpati; there the Vedas and sacri-fices in bodily form (मूर्तिमन्तः) as also the sages worship (उपासते) Prajāpati; there gods and Cakracaras offer sacrifices (यजन्ते क्रतुभिः) 3. 83. 72-73; (3) There are three Agnikuṇḍas at Prayāga from where the Jāhnavī, followed by all the other तीर्थस्, flows 3. 83. 69; (4) At Prayāga, the daughter of Tapana (the sun), i. e. the Yamunā, meets the Gaṅgā 3. 83. 70; (5) The land between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā is known as the जघन (part below the navel) of the earth; Prayāga is known to the sages as the उपस्थ, i. e. the end of this जघन (गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्यं पृथिव्या जघनं स्मृतम् । प्रयागं जघनस्यान्तम् उपस्थम् ऋषयो विदुः ॥ ) 3. 83. 71 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 75: स्त्रीरूपायाः पृथिव्याः … जघ-नं नाभेर् अधोभागः; on 3. 85. 76 where he reads जघमस्थानम्: जघ-नस्य स्थानम् अवस्थानं समाप्तिर् अन्त इति यावत् तद् एवोपस्थम् । ); (6) At Pra-yāga are present ten thousand and sixty crores of तीर्थस् 3. 83. 79; according to Aṅgiras ten thousand तीर्थस् and three crores of them gather at Prayāga on the new moon day of the month of Māgha (समा-गच्छन्ति माघ्यां तु प्रयागे) 13. 26. 35; (7) Prayāga finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 18, 2. F. Events: (1) Epic: (i) The Pāṇḍavas bathed there; they lived there and practised the severest austerities (ऊषुर् आप्लुत्य गात्राणि तपश् चातस्थुर् उत्तमम्); at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā the sinless, high-souled (विपाप्मानो महात्मानः) Pāṇḍa-vas gave riches to Brāhmaṇas 3. 93. 5, 6; (ii) Among other holy places Ambā visited Prayāga; she bathed there and practised severe austerities 5. 187. 28; (2) Mytho-logical: Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) formerly offered there a sacrifice 3. 85. 14; 1. 50. 1.  [See Prasravaṇāni trīṇi]

Prayāga m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of war, Prayāga warriors were among those who stood at the neck of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of Pāṇḍavas (प्रयागाश् च … ग्रीवायां) 6. 46. 46.
प्रवरा: Pravarā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13 (for other details see Palāśinī).
प्रवेणी: Praveṇī f.: Name of a river. Situated in the south (दक्षिणस्याम्) 3. 86. 1; to its north are forests of ascetics (प्रवेण्युत्तरपार्श्वे तु … तापसानाम् अरण्यानि) 3. 86. 8; listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are known as mothers of the fire-hearths, i. e. on whose banks sacrifices were performed (धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (for Nī. see Kapilā).
प्रशस्ता: Praśastā f.: Name of a river. Located in the south (cf. 3. 117. 18); described as most holy (पुण्यतमा) and flowing to the ocean (समुद्रगा) 3. 118. 2; Yudhiṣṭhira visited it along with his brothers and, after bathing there (आप्लुत्य), he satis-fied manes and gods (संतर्पयाम् आस पितॄन् सुरांश् च) and gave riches to the prominent among the Brāhmaṇas; from there he went to the river Godāvarī 3. 118. 3.
प्रस्रवणानि: Prasravaṇāni trīṇi nt. (pl.): Three streams, not named, on the mountain Ārcīka. Described as holy (पुण्यानि); Yudhi-ṣṭhira was advised to go round them and bathe there as much as he desired (यथाकामम् उपस्पृश) 3. 125. 15 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 125. 18: त्रीणि प्रस्रवणानीति च प्रयागम् । … यथाकामम् इत्य् अस्य काशीप्रयागसेविनां चन्द्रतीर्थसेवङम् ऐच्छिकम् इतरेषाम् अत्यावश्यकम् इति भा-वः । ).
प्लक्षप्रस्रवण: Plakṣaprasravaṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the Himavant moun-tain 9. 53. 9, 11; (सो ऽवतीर्याचलश्रेष्ठात् प्लक्षप्रस्रवणात्) 9. 53. 33; it is the source of the river Sarasvatī (प्रभवं च सर-स्वत्याः) 9. 53. 11; also cf. 3. 82. 5. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 9. 53. 10; auspicious (शुभ) 9. 53. 33; an excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 53. 10. C. Epic event: Balarāma in his तीर्थयात्रा visited it when he ascended the mountain Himavant and was filled with wonder on seeing it; from there he went to the Kārapacana तीर्थ 9. 53. 9-11; later he descended from the mountain and the तीर्थ 9. 53. 33. [See Plakṣarāja, Plakṣāvataraṇa]
प्लक्षराज: Plakṣarāja m.: The big Plakṣa tree, not named. Situated near the तीर्थ of Soma 9. 42. 38; God Kārtikeya always lived there in person 9. 42. 41. [See Plakṣaprasravaṇa and Plakṣāvataraṇa]
प्लक्षावतरण: Plakṣāvataraṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ, also called Yamunātīrtha (3. 129. 13; 9. 48. 10). A. Location: In the north (उदीच्याम्) 3. 88. 1, on the river Yamunā (यमुना-तीर्थम् उच्यते) 3. 129. 13. B. Descrip-tion: Most holy (पुण्यतम) 3. 88. 3; auspicious (शिव) 3. 88. 3; excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 48. 15; called the gate of the heaven (नाकपृष्ठस्य द्वारम्) 3. 129. 13. C. Holiness: (1) Brāhmaṇas go to this तीर्थ for their अवभृथ bath at the end of their sacrifices performed with the help of the Brāhmaṇas hailing from the river Sara-svatī (यत्र सारस्वतैर् इष्ट्वा गच्छन्त्य् अवभृथं द्विजाः) 3. 88. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 90. 4: सारस्वतैः सरस्वत्यां प्राप्तैः; अत्र सारस्वतैर् यज्ञैर् ईजानाः परमर्षयः … । गच्छन्त्य् अवभृथा-प्लवम् ॥ ) 3. 129. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 14: सारस्वतैर् ब्राह्मणैः ऋत्विग्भिर् यज्ञैर् ईजानाः); (2) By bathing at this तीर्थ one sees all the worlds (अत्रोपस्पृश्य राजेन्द्र सर्वा̆ल् लोकान् प्रपश्यति) 3. 129. 17, 20; (3) By bathing at this तीर्थ one is purified of bad deeds (पूयते दुष्कृताच् चैव समुपस्पृश्य) 3. 129. 17. D. Epic events: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira bathed at this तीर्थ with his brothers; by this act and due to his austerities, he was able to see all the worlds; he was also able to see Arjuna (इहस्थः … पश्यामि श्वेतवाहनम्) 3. 129. 19 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 19: इहस्थः यमुनान्तर्गतप्लक्षावतरणस्थः); (2) Balarāma visited the Yamunātīrtha; he bath-ed there and gave wealth to the twice-born; from there he went to the Ādityatīrtha 9. 48. 10, 15-16. E. Mythological and Past events: (1) Varuṇa, son of Aditi, performed a Rājasūya at the Yamunātīrtha after con-quering human and divine (opponents) 9. 48. 11-12; (2) King Marutta, helped by Saṃ-varta, offered there an excellent सत्र 3. 129. 16; (3) Bharata, after conquering the earth righteously (धर्मेणावाप्य मेदिनीम्), often performed horse sacrifices using each time a black and speckled horse (मेध्यम् अश्वम् अवासृजत् । असकृत् कृष्णसारङ्गम्) 3. 129. 15. [See Yāmuna2, Plakṣaprasra-vaṇa, Plakṣarāja]
पत्तन: Pattana nt.: Name of a city (?) One of the kings who came for Drau-padī's स्वयंवर is called Pattanādhipati (ruler of Pattana) (पत्तनाधिपतिस् तथा) 1. 177. 12.
पर्णशाला: Parṇaśālā f.: Name of a village (ग्राम). A. Location: Located in Madhya-deśa, between the rivers Gaṅgā and Ya-munā, and at the foot of the mountain Yāmuna (मध्यदेशे … । गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्ये यामुनस्य गिरेर् अधः) 13. 67. 3. B. Description: Big (महन्त्) 13. 67. 3; famous (विख्यात) 13. 67. 4; pleasing (र-मणीय) 13. 67. 4; C. Characteristic: It was a settlement of the Brāhmaṇas, most of them known for their learning (ग्रामो ब्राह्मणानां बभूव ह) 13. 67. 3; (विद्वांसस् तत्र भूयिष्ठा ब्राह्मणाश् चावसंस् तदा) 13. 67. 4; hence also refe-rred to as Brāhmaṇagrāma 13. 67. 6. D. Past event: Yama once told one of his men to go to the Brāhmaṇagrāma and br-ing from there a Brāhmaṇa named Śarmin belonging to the Agastya गोत्र (अगस्त्यं गोत्रतश् चापि नामतश् चापि शर्मिणम्) 13. 67. 5-6.
पाञ्चालनगर: Pāñcālanagara nt.: The capital town Kāmpilya of the southern Pāñcāla country where Drupada ruled. The Pāṇḍavas, after the death of Baka in Ekacakrā, proceeded to Pāñcālanagara (पाञ्चालनगरम् अभिगताः) 1. 90. 80; Vyāsa advised the Pāṇḍavas to go to Pāñcālnagara where they would get Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) for their wife (पाञ्चालनगरं तस्मात् प्रविशध्वं महाबलाः) 1. 157. 15. [See Kāmpilya, Śiśumārapura]
पिङ्गाया: Piṅgāyā āśramaḥ m.: A hermitage so called. By bathing at the आश्रम of Piṅgā one was freed of all sins (पिङ्गायाश् चाश्रमे स्नात्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते) 13. 26. 52.
पिच्छण्ड: Picchaṇḍa nt.: Name of a town. Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1) before the Rājasūya, subjugated Picchaṇḍa just by sending envoys and made the citi-zens pay tribute (पिच्छण्डं … । दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 47.
पितॄणाम्: Pitṝṇām āśramaḥ m.: A hermitage so called. The तीर्थस् known as Marudgaṇa and Vaivasvata were probably located near this आश्रम; if one who is pure bathes in those तीर्थस् himself becomes as holy as a तीर्थ (तीर्थभूतो भवेन् नरः) 13. 26. 37.
पुरिका: Purikā f.: Name of a town. Described as glorious (श्रीमती); a very cruel king called Paurika once lived in the city Purikā (पुरिकायां पुरि पुरा श्रीम-त्यां पौरिको नृपः । परहिंसारुचिः क्रूरो बभूव पुरुषाधमः ॥ ) 12. 112. 3.
पुलिन्दनगर: Pulindanagara nt.: Name of a town. Bhīma, in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1) before the Rājasūya, subjugated Sukumāra and Sumitra at Pulindanagara; described as a big town (महन्त्) 2. 26. 10.
पैलगार्ग्यस्य: Pailagārgyasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। One of the holy places where the Kāśī princess Ambā lived to practise austerities in order to be able to kill Bhīṣma 5. 187. 27; she bathed at these holy places day and night and practised severe austerities (आश्र-मं पुण्यशीलानां तापसानां महात्म-नाम् ॥ तत्र पुण्येषु देशेषु साप्लुताङ्गी दिवानिशम् । व्यचरत् काशिकन्या सा) 5. 187. 24; (एतेषु तीर्थेषु … आप्लावयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 28.
पोतन: Potana nt.: Name of a town. Established by the royal sage Aśmaka, son of the wife of Kalmāṣapāda begotten by sage Vasiṣṭha (अश्मको नाम राजर्षिः पोतनं यो न्यवेशयत्) 1. 168. 25.
प्रमाणकोटि: Pramāṇakoṭi f.: Name of a place on the river Gaṅgā. A place on the river Gaṅgā where at a suitable place Duryodhana once got ready rest houses made of garments and कम्बलस् for water sports; there Duryo-dhana bound Bhīma, who fell asleep due to fatigue, by fetters made of creepers and threw him in water (ततो जलविहारा-र्थं कारयाम् आस भारत । चेलकम्बल-वेश्मानि … । प्रमाणकोट्याम् उद्देशं स्थलं किंचिद् उपेत्य च ॥ … प्रमाण-कोट्यां वाषार्थी सुष्वापारुह्य तत् स्थ-लम् ॥ ); he also tried to kill Bhīma there by serpent bites and by mixing poison in his food 1. 119. 29-30, 32, 34, 36-41 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 128. 33; प्रमाणकोट्यां गङ्गायां प्रदेशविशेषे । स्थलं किंचिद् अर्धं जले ऽर्धं स्थले च क्रीडागारम्); these incidents are referred to on various occasions: (1) by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary of the epic narrative (प्रमाण-कोट्यां संसुप्तं पुनर् बद्ध्वा वृकोद-रम् । तोयेषु भीमं गङ्गायाः प्रक्षिप्य पुरम् आव्रजत्) 1. 55. 9-12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 61. 11: प्रमाणकोट्यां गङ्गायास् तीर्थविशेषे); (ii) by Draupadī while re-counting to Kṛṣṇa Duryodhana's misdeeds (प्रमाणकोट्यां विश्वस्तं तथा सुप्तं  … । गङ्गायां प्रक्षिप्य पुनर् आव्रजत् ॥ ) 3. 13. 71-77 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 12. 82: प्रमाणकोट्यां प्रमाणाख्यो गङ्गातीर-स्थो वटविशेषस् तत्प्रदेशे); (iii) By Bhīma while proclaiming the misdeeds of the Kauravas at the time of Duḥśāsana's death (प्रमाणकोट्यां शयनम्) 8. 61. 12; (iv) By Bhīma while enumerating to Yudhiṣṭhira the misdeeds of Duryodhana (सर्पोत्सर्गस्य शयने विषदानस्य भोजने प्रमाणकोट्यां पातस्य) 9. 55. 20.
प्राग्ज्योतिष: Prāgjyotiṣa m.: Name of a famous city (called पुर 2. 42. 7; 3. 13. 26; 5. 47. 74; नगर 14. 74. 3, 6). A. Location: Situated in the east; it was encircled by the Kirātas, Cīnas and other warrior tribes living near the sea coast (स किरातैश् च चीनैश् च वृतः प्राग्ज्योतिषो ऽभवत् । अन्यैश् च बहुभिर् योधैः साग-रानूपवासिभिः ॥ ) 2. 23. 19 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 22. 9; प्राग्ज्योतिषं पूर्वसमुद्र-तीरस्थं नगरविशेषम्); from there Arjuna proceeded to the north (प्रयास्यामि दिशं धनदरक्षिताम्) 2. 23. 4; 2. 24. 1. B. Description: Beautiful (रम्य) 12. 326. 85; difficult of access (दुर्ग) 5. 47. 74; fierce (घोर) 5. 47. 74; insuperable (असह्य) 5. 47. 74; full of wealth of different kinds (नानाधनसमन्वित) 12. 326. 85; the city of Asuras (असुराणां पुरम्) 5. 47. 74. C. Its rulers: Governed by Bhagadatta (2. 23. 18) and then by his son Vajradatta (14. 74. 1); hence they are called Prāgjyoti-ṣādhipa (Bhagadatta) 2. 47. 12; 5. 164. 35; (Vajradatta) 14. 75. 16. D. Epic events: (1) Arjuna attacked Prāgjyotiṣa during his expedition before the Rājasūya and then proceeded to the north 2. 23. 17; 2. 24. 1; Arjuna's battle with Bhagadatta alluded to in 5. 164. 35-37; (2) King Bhagadatta of Prāgjyotiṣa brought fine-bred horses as tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 47. 12; (3) Once, during his battle with Kṛṣṇa, Śālva, riding his Saubha which could move at will (सौभं कामगमम्), suddenly went as far as Prāgjyotiṣa 3. 23. 9; (4) The excellent horse of the Aśvamedha sacri-fice, while roaming, went to Prāgjyotiṣa 14. 74. 1. E. Past events: (1) Powerful Naraka, son of Bhūmi, carried away the jewelled earrings of Aditi to Prāgjyotiṣa (महाबलो नरकस् तत्र भौमो जहारा-दित्या मणिकुण्डले शुभे) 5. 47. 74; (2) Nārāyaṇa prophesied to Nārada that at the close of the junction of Dvāpara and Kali (12. 326. 82) he would be born at Mathurā; he would then kill Naraka, Mura and Pīṭha and carry away the wealth of Prāgjyotiṣa to Kuśasthalī (प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरं रम्यं नानाधनसमन्वितम् । कुशस्थलीं नयिष्यामि) 12. 326. 85; Naraka, and his Dānavas, could not arrest Kṛṣṇa who had gone to Prāgjyotiṣa 5. 128. 44; (3) When Kṛṣṇa and the other Sātvata heroes had gone to Prāgjyotiṣa, Śiśupāla burnt Dvā-rakā 2. 42. 7; (4) By killing Nisunda and Naraka, Kṛṣṇa once again made the way to Prāgjyotiṣa safe (कृतः क्षेमः पुनः पन्थाः पुरं प्राग्ज्योतिषं प्रति) 3. 13. 26.
पञ्चकर्पट: Pañcakarpaṭa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Nakula subjugated them in his expedi-tion to the west (प्रतीचीं नकुलो राजन् 2. 23. 10; वासुदेवजिताम् आशाम् 2. 29. 1) before the Rājasūya (वशे चक्रे … माल-वान् पञ्चकर्पटान्) 2. 29. 6.
पटच्चर: Paṭaccara m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; also called Rāṣṭra. A. Location: Mentioned among the Rāṣṭras or Janapadas situated around Kurus (राष्ट्राणि … जनपदा … परितः कुरून् । … शूरसेनाः पटच्चराः) 4. 1. 8, 9; mentioned among those people who, afraid of Jarāsandha, had fled to the south from the north (पतच्चराः । … तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परित्यज्य भयार्-दिताः … दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 25, 27; Sahadeva subjugated Paṭa-ccaras south of Indraprastha (प्रययु दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; also 2. 23. 9; see below Epic events No. 1). B. Des-cription: Pleasing (रमणीय) 4. 1. 8; (रम्य) 4. 1. 9; having ample food (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; protected (गुप्त) 4. 1. 8. C. Epic events; (1) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya, defeated Paṭaccaras (व्यजयत् स पटच्चरान्) 2. 28. 4; (2) On the second day of the war, Yudhiṣṭhira along with Paṭaccara and other warriors formed the ‘back’ (पृष्ठम्) of the Krauñcāruṇa (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍa-vas 6. 46. 47. D. They figure in the characterization of a king: A certain king (not named) in the Pāṇdava army, is referred to as ‘killer of the Paṭaccaras’; he was driven by parrot-coloured horses (तं पटच्चरहन्तारं शुकवर्णावहन् ःअयाः) 7. 22. 53; (तं पटच्चरहन्तारम्) 7. 24. 32.
पत्तिपञ्जक: Pattipañjaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षि-ना … ) 6. 10. 56; (सतियः पत्तिपञ्जकाः) 6. 10. 62.
पनीतक: Panītaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37; गोपराष्ट्राः पनीतकाः) 6. 10. 42.
परतङ्गण: Parataṅgaṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (आथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56; तङ्गणाः परतङ्गणाः) 6. 10. 63; but they are also said to have lived on a mountain between Meru and Mandara, near the river Śailodā and enjoyed the pleasing shade of bamboo trees (मेरुमन्दरयोर् मध्ये शैलो-दाम् अभितो नदीम् । ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्याम् उपासते ॥ ) 2. 48. 2. B. Epic events: (1) Their kings brought as tribute for the Rājasūya gold called ‘पिपीलिक’, given as boon by ants, in heaps to be measured by द्रोणस् (ते वै पिपीलिकं नाम वरदत्तं पिपीलिकैः । जातरूपं द्रोणमेयम् अहार्षुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः) 2. 48. 4; (2) On the sixth day of war, they and other warriors were stationed on the right side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 49-50.
परमकाम्बोज: Paramakāmboja m. (pl.): Name of a people. Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम्) 2. 23. 9; 2. 24. 1 and the north-west (प्रागुत्तरां दिशम् 2. 24. 23) defeated Paramakāmbojas (परमकाम्बोजान् व्यजयत्) 2. 24. 24. [See Kāmboja].
परवल्लक: Paravallaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (लाङ्गलाः परवल्लकाः) 6. 10. 55.
परसंचरक: Parasaṃcaraka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षि-णा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (प्रोष्ठाः परसंचर-कास् तथा) 6. 10. 60.
पर्वतान्तरवासिन्: Parvatāntaravāsin m. (pl.): General characterization of people living in the valleys. They came for the Rājasūya of Yudhi-ṣṭhira with large tributes of various kinds but were stopped at the gate (पर्वतान्-तरवासिनः … द्वारि वारितान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्य नानारूपान् अनेकशः) 2. 47. 19-20; (बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 25; their tributes consisting of asses, woolen and other kinds of cloth, soft deer-skins, long swords and other weapons, sharp axes produced in the west, and various juices and per-fumes described in 2. 47. 21-28.
पलदाश: Paladāśa m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of the war, they and other warriors stood on the left side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (पल-दाशाश् च भारत … वामं पार्श्वं समा-श्रिताः) 6. 46. 51.
पशु: Paśu m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern mleccha people of the Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … ) 6. 10. 63; (काश्मी-राः पशुभिः सह) 6. 10. 66.
पशुप: Paśupa m. (pl.): Characterization of a people. A. Location: They lived between the mountains Meru and Mandara, along the river Śailodā and enjoyed the delightful shade of the bamboos and reeds 2. 48. 2-3. B. Epic events: Their kings brought as tribute for the Rājasūya gold called पिपीलिक, given as boon by the ants, in lumps to be measured by द्रोणस् 2. 48. 4 (for citations see Parataṅgaṇa).
पशुभूमि: Paśubhūmi f. (sg.): Name of a land. Bhīma in his expedition to the east (भीमसेनस् तथा प्राचीम् 2. 23. 9; 2. 26. 1; पूर्वदेशम् 2. 26. 9) before the Rāja-śūya conquered the whole of the Paśu-bhūmi (विजिग्ये … पशुभूमिं च सर्वशः) 2. 27. 7-8.
पश्चिमानूपक: Paścimānūpaka m. (pl.): Name of a people (living near watery places ?) They lived in the west; mentioned by Drupada among the peoples whose kings were to be approached by Yudhiṣṭhira for help in war (ये नृपाः । … पश्चिमानूपकाश् च ये) 5. 4. 15.
पह्लव: Pahlava (Pallava) m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Mentioned by Saṃjaya while listing the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबो-ध) 6. 10. 37, 5 (पल्लवाश् चर्मखण्डि-काः) 6. 10. 46, and also while listing the northern म्लेच्छ people of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … तुखाराश् च पल्लव … ) 6. 10. 63, 66; they lived by the gulf of the western ocean (प्रतीचीम् 2. 23. 10; 2. 29. 19); (सागरकुक्षिस्थान्) 2. 29. 15; also lived in the caves of mountains (पल्लवा गिरिगह्वराः) 6. 10. 66. B. Origin: Created by Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, from her tail (असृजत् पह्लवान् पुच्छात्) 1. 165. 35. C. Characterization: Called म्लेच्छ पेओप्ले 6. 10. 63; very cruel म्ले-च्छस् (म्लेच्छान् परमदारुणान्) 2. 29. 15; they lived in countries but led the life of दस्युस् (सर्वे विषयवासिनः । … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15. D. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedition to the west (प्रतीचीम् 2. 23. 10; 2. 29. 11; वासुदेव-जिताम् आशाम् 2. 29. 1) before the Rājasūya brought Pahlavas under control (पह्लवान्  … अनयद् वशम्) 2. 29. 15; (2) The Kṣatriyas among them brought wealth by hundreds as tribute for the Rājasūya (पह्लवैः सह … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 14, 16; (3) Drupada suggested to Yudhiṣṭhira to send quickly messengers to the kings of Pahlavas and others for help in war (दूता गच्छन्तु शीघ्रगाः) 5. 4. 8, 25; (शकानां पह्लवा-नां च … ये नृपाः) 5. 4. 15 (but they joined the side of the Kauravas; see the next); (4) When the army of the Kauravas got ready for war, Kṛpa, along with Pahlavas and others guarded the army on the northern side (पह्लवैश् च … चमूम् उत्तरतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 13. E. Past events: Māndhātṛ asked Indra about the धर्म of the Pahlavas and others and how they should be controlled by kings like him (पह्लवाश् … कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्था-प्याः) 12. 65. 13, 15; Indra then instructed Māndhātṛ in the धर्म of Pahlavas 12. 65. 17-22.
पांशु: Pāṃśu(Pāṃsu)rāṣṭra n. (sg.), m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (अश्मकाः पांसुराष्ट्राश् च) 6. 10. 42. B. Epic events: King Vasudāna of Pāṃśurāṣṭra offered as tribute for the Rājasūya twenty-six elephants and two thousand horses, wearing gold garlands, and who were speedy, strong and of proper age (पांशु-राष्ट्राद् वसुदानो राजा षड्विंशतिं गजान् । अश्वानां च सहस्रे द्वे राजन् काञ्चनमा-लिनां । जवसत्त्वोपपन्नानां वयःस्था-नां नराधिप) 2. 48. 26-27. C. A king of Pāṃśurāṣṭra (not named; Vasudāna ?) called पांसुराष्ट्राधिप 5. 4. 17.
पाञ्चाल: Pāñcāla m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada or a Rāṣṭra and its people; Pāñcālas are sometimes identified with Sṛñjayas, but also often mentioned separately from them. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; तत्रेमे कुरूपाञ्चालाः) 6. 10. 37; (पाञ्चालाः कौशिजाश् चैव) 6. 10. 40; called Janapada also in 4. 1. 9. and Rāṣṭra in 1. 128. 7; 4. 1. 8; listed by Arjuna among the Janapadas lying around the Kuru country (सन्ति रम्या जनपदा … परितः कुरून् । पाञ्चालाश् चेदिमत्स्याश् च) 4. 1. 9; to the east of Indraprastha (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति) 2. 26. 1; 2. 23. 9; (also see Epic events No. 11 below); the way of Pāṇḍavas from Dvaitavana (3. 295. 2-3, 5) to the Matsya country lay between Pāñcāla to the north and Daśārṇa to the south (उत्तरेण दशार्णांस् ते पाञ्चालान् दक्षि-णेन तु) 4. 5. 3; the तीर्थ Utpalāvata was situated in Pāñcāla country 3. 85. 11; Pāñcāla was divided by Droṇa into nor-thern and southern Pāñcāla, the dividing line being the river Bhāgīrathī (राजासि दक्षिने कूले भागीरथ्याहम् उत्तरे) 1. 128. 12; southern Pāñcāla country lay to the south of Gaṅgā and up to Carmaṇvatī river (दक्षिणांश् चैव पाञ्चालान् यावच् चर्मण्-वती नदी) 1. 128. 15, 12. B. Origin: All Pāñcālas traced their origin to Duḥṣanta and Parameṣṭhin (तथेमे सर्वपाञ्चाला दुःषन्तपरमेष्ठिनोः । अन्वयाः) 1. 89. 29. C. Description: (1) Country: pleasing (रमणीय), protected (गुप्त) and rich in harvest (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; alms were easily available in the Pāñcāla country (सुभिक्षाश् चैव पाञ्चालाः) 1. 156. 7; (2) People: high-sould (महात्मन्) 5. 168. 11; 7. 132. 38; 8. 31. 51; 8. 43. 53; a certain Brāhmaṇa told the assembly of Kurus that Pāñcālas (as well as Kurus) knew the eternal धर्म; they followed the ancient धर्म; Pāñcālas were as good as brahminhood incarnate (कुरवः सह-पाञ्चालाः … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्; धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति; आ पाञ्चाल-भ्यः कुरवो … जानन्ति धर्मं; ब्राह्मं पाञ्चालाः) 8. 30. 60-62; 73, 75; Pāñcālas could guess correctly everything when only a part was told to them (अर्धोक्ताः कुरुपाञ्चालाः (जानन्ति)) 8. 30. 79; (3) Warriors: having arms as long as a परिघ (परिघबाहु) 6. 114. 107; heroic (शूर) 6. 114. 107; 7. 97. 51; 7. 101. 68; 8. 8. 19; 8. 32. 38; 8. 56. 47; (वीर) 7. 55. 9; of great energy (महौजस्) 2. 72. 29; 3. 48. 6; 7. 132. 41; energetic (तरस्विन्) 8. 51. 99; great archers (महेष्वास) 6. 84. 3; 8. 51. 95; 9. 6. 40; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 5. 168. 11; 7. 85. 28; 8. 51. 95; tamers of enemies, they were always determined to defeat the enemies (ते नित्यम् उदिता जेतुं युद्धे शत्रून् अरिंदमाः) 8. 51. 98; tormentors of adversaries (परंतप) 8. 60. 26; arrogant in wars (युद्धदुर्मद) 5. 162. 22; 8. 43. 3; who have done valorous deeds (पराक्रान्त) 5. 52. 2; excellent among those who wield weapons (सर्वशस्त्र-भृतां वराः) 8. 43. 22; tigers among men (नरव्याघ्र) 8. 43. 61; 8. 44. 8; 9. 1. 30; 9. 7. 42; compared with Indra (शक्रोपम) 7. 133. 4; difficult to resist, not easy to attack them (दुर्निवार्य, दुरासद) 7. 31. 38; they fought like agitated elephants (संरब्धा इव कुञ्जराः) 5. 168. 11; not afraid while fighting (न त्व् एव भीताः) 8. 51. 95; not running away, rarely showing their backs (अपलायिन्) 8. 43. 59; (कथं-चित् स्युः पराङ्मुखाः) 8. 51. 95; their great warriors did not care for death (न हि मृत्युं महेष्वासा गणयन्ति महा-रथाः) 8. 51. 95; in war they closely followed the आर्यधर्म (आर्यधर्मसं-रब्ध) 7. 31. 38; cruel (क्रूर) 7. 30. 6; they are also called inauspicious (अशिव) and capable of doing cruel deeds (क्रूर-कर्मन्) 7. 7. 32; mean and betrayers of friends and teacher, they could stray away from धर्म (पाञ्चालाश् चलिता धर्मात् क्षुद्रा मित्रगुरुद्रुहः) 7. 169. 18. D. Epic events: Drupada became the king of the Uttara Pāñcāla after his father's death 1. 121. 10; (2) Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas attacked the Pāñcālas and crushed the capital town of Drupada (ममृदुस् तस्य नगरं द्रुपदस्य) 1. 128. 4; (3) After his defeat, Drupada was allowed by Droṇa to rule over the southern Pāñcālas, with Kāmpilya as its capital 1. 128. 12, 15; (4) After their escape from Vāraṇāvata, Pāṇḍavas passed through many countries, one of them being Pāñcāla 1. 144. 2; (5) A certain Brāhmaṇa told Pāṇḍavas about the स्वयंवर to be held in the Pāñcāla country 1. 153. 7; (6) When Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna arose from the sacrificial fire, delighted Pāñcālas shouted ‘good, good’ ( … प्रणेदुः पाञ्चालाः प्रहृष्टाः साधु साध्व् इति); an invisible being in the sky (महद् भूतम् अदृश्यं खेचरं) declar-ed that Dhṛṣṭadyumna would remove the fear of the Pāñcālas and bring them fame 1. 155. 39-40; (7) When Pāñcālas heard the heavenly voice at the rise of Draupadī from the sacrificial altar, they roared like a horde of lions; the earth could not bear their burden who were filled with joy (प्रणेदुः सिंहसंघवत् । न चैतान् हर्षसंपूर्णान् इयं सेहे वसौंधरा) 1. 155. 46; (8) Kuntī suggested to Pāṇḍavas to go to Pāñcāla 1. 156. 6; Vyāsa too advised them to go to the town of Pāñcālas (Kāmpilya) for the स्वयंवर (पाञ्चाल-नगरं … प्रविशध्वम्) 1. 157. 15; trave-lling Brāhmaṇas advised Pāṇḍavas to do the same 1. 175. 5; (9) Pāṇḍavas started for the southern Pāñcālas and reached it 1. 176. 2, 5; this event is referred to earlier in the summary narration of the Mahābhārata in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan 1. 2. 86, and again at 1. 55. 21; (10) The southern Pāñcālas, afraid of Jarā-sandha, left their land and went further south; they also fled in different directions (दक्षिणा ये च पाञ्चालाः … तथोत्तरां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ … तथैव सर्वपाञ्चाला जरासन्धभयार्दिताः ॥ स्वराष्ट्रं सं-परित्यज्य विद्रुताः सर्वतोदिशम् ॥ ) 2. 13. 26-28; (11) Bhīmasena, in his expedi-tion to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; also 2. 23. 9); before the Rājasūya, won over Pāñcālas by various means of conciliation (पाञ्चालान् विविधो-पायैः सान्त्वयाम् आस) 2. 26. 3; this event is referred to later in 4. 5. 19 where, however, it is said that he defeated them in battle (पाञ्चालान् … संग्रामे भीमसेनोऽजयत्); Pāñcālas did not pay tribute for Rājasūya because they had marriage-relationship with Pāṇḍavas (वैवाहिकेन पाञ्चालाः) 2. 48. 42; (12) Vidura told Kauravas that Pāñcālas would not forgive the torture to Draupadī (in the Sabhā); Arjuna, prote-cted by Pāñcālas, would invade them 2. 72. 29-30; (13) Pāñcālas meeting the Pāṇḍavas in the forest (3. 13. 2) referred to in the narration of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 106; (14) Drau-padī complained to Kṛṣṇa that though Pāñcālas were alive Kauravas desired to treat Draupadī as a Dāsī 3. 13. 56; (15) Dhṛtarāṣṭra was afraid that later Pāñ-cālas, protected by Kṛṣṇa, would burn the Kaurava army 3. 48. 6; (16) Bhīma feared that if Arjuna (who had departed to get weapons) was dead, Pāñcālas, Pāṇḍavas and the rest would perish 3. 49. 6; (17) Bhīma told Draupadī that Pāñcā-las, with the support of Arjuna, would not be afraid of even gods if they had to fight with them 3. 79. 20; (18) Before the अज्ञातवास, Yudhiṣṭhira asked the women who attended on Draupadī, as also cooks and chief cooks, to go to the Pāñcāla country 4. 4. 4; (19) According to Drau-padī, the affliction she had to suffer while living as Sairandhrī meant insult to Kurus and Pāñcālas 4. 19. 11; (20) Karṇa told Bhīṣma that Pāṇḍavas were claiming their share because they depen-ded on the force of Pāñcālas and Matsyas (राज्यम् इच्छन्ति पैतृकम् । बलम् आश्रित्य मत्स्यानां पाञ्चालानां च) 5. 21. 11; (21) Yudhiṣṭhira could have resorted to war without going into exile since the Pāñcālas were always available to him for guidance (नित्यं पाञ्चालाः सचिवास् तवे-मे) 5. 27. 17; (22) By avoiding war, Yudhiṣṭhira wished Pāñcālas to meet Kurus with a smile; he desired both of them to remain uninjured and, well-disposed, live in peace (अक्षतान् कुरुपाञ्चालान् पश्येम … सर्वे सुमनसस् तात शाम्याम) 5. 31. 21-22; (23) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍavas were waiting for the orders of Yudhiṣṭhira (राज्ञो मुखम् उदीक्षन्ते); they, riding chariots, greeted him when he approached them 5. 49. 4-7; Saṃjaya also told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Pāñcā-las did not honour him and that they des-pised him (नार्हन्ति पाञ्चालाश् … सर्वे त्वाम् अवजानते) 5. 53. 17; (24) Pāñcālas mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among those who sided with Pāṇḍavas 5. 56. 33; (25) Duryodhana assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Pāñcālas would be attacked by his chariot-fighters with arrows 5. 56. 42; he also told him that he would soon hear Pāñcālas defeated by him 5. 60. 25; (26) Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍavas counted on Dhṛṣṭadyumna's fortitude and valour 5. 56. 51; (27) Karṇa told Duryodhana that the ब्रह्मास्त्र he had obtained from Paraśurāma was still with him and hence due to the favour of the ऋषि (Paraśurāma) he would kill Pāñcā-las and the rest in no time; that was his responsibility (ततस् तद् अस्त्रम् मम सावशेषं । तस्मात् समर्थो ऽस्मि ममैष भारः ॥ … तम् ऋषिप्रसादम् अवाप्य पाञ्-चाल° … । निहत्य) 5. 61. 4-5 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 62. 4: सावशेषं मम आयुर् अस्ति । अतो ऽन्तकालस्यानुपस्थितत्वात् तद् अस्त्रं ममास्तीत्य् अहं समर्थो ऽस्मि); (28) Yudhiṣṭhira, although backed by Pāñcālas and others, chose to ask for five villages 5. 70. 14; (29) Even when Pāñcālas were alive, Draupadī was looked upon as a दासी in the Sabhā of the wretched Kauravas 5. 80. 25; (30) Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that the Pāñcālas and others would consecrate him as king; Pāñcālas would follow him in his procession 5. 138. 16-17, 23; (31) Vidura told Kuntī that Yudhiṣṭhira was supported by Pāñ-cālas 5. 142. 3; there was nothing more painful to Kuntī than Pāñcālas and others fighting with Bhāratas 5. 142. 3, 12; (32) When Pāñcālas proceeded towards Kuru-kṣetra, they were led by Bhīmasena 5. 149. 50; (33) Duryodhana and others were to kill Pāñcālas in battle 5. 162. 22; Droṇa was to burn Pāñcālas (प्रधक्ष्यति स पाञ्चा-लान्) 5. 164. 20; Pāñcālas would run in all directions when they encountered Karṇa 5. 165. 21; (34) Pāñcālas and Prabhadrakas formed the army of Śikhaṇḍin 5. 168. 3; (35) Hiraṇyavarman's friends wanted to kill Drupada and instal another king in the Pāñcāla country if Śikhaṇḍin proved to be a girl 5. 191. 8; (36) Saṃjaya reported that Bhīṣma showered arrows on Pāñcālas 6. 15. 25; on the first day of war, Bhīṣma's chariot moved very often among Pāñcālas and he killed them 6. 45. 4, 54; (37) On the second day, Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa to take him to Bhīṣma since Droṇa and others, protected by Bhīṣma, would kill Pāñcālas 6. 48. 15 (13); Pāñcālas cheered loudly when Dhṛṣṭadyumna cut off a fierce and shining arrow discharged at him by Droṇa 6. 49. 13; Bhīma was honoured by Pāñcā-las when he killed Kaliṅga warriors 6. 50. 110 (108); (38) On the third day, Pāñcālas stood in the middle of the Ardha-candravyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 52. 14, 10; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya how the Pāñcālas fared against Bhīṣma 6. 55. 2; seeing the river of blood made to flow by Arjuna's sharp arrows, Pāñcālas delight-fully raised a loud roar 6. 55. 126, (121-125); (39) On the fourth day, the chief warriors of Pāñcālas stood at the same place of the same व्यूह as they did on the previous day 6. 56. 11; when Bhīṣma and others marched to help Bhagadatta, Pāñcālas and others chased them; since Bhīṣma did not like to continue fighting with Ghaṭotkaca, Pāñcālas and others he thought of declaring the end of the war for that day 6. 60. 64, 68; (40) On the fifth day, although Pāñcālas were getting killed by Bhīṣma, they rushed at him with spirited mind (आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा) 6. 68. 31; (41) On the sixth day, Bhīṣma put to death the armies of Pāñcālas with arrows the joints of which were smooth 6. 75. 57; (42) On the seventh day, Droṇa scattered away Pāñcālas (व्यध-मत्) 6. 82. 38; (43) On the eighth day, Bhīṣma felled down great Pāñcāla archers, but not afraid of death (त्यक्त्वा मृत्युकृतं भयम्), they attacked Bhīṣma; he cut off their hands and heads and broke their chariots; those who fought from horse-backs also lost their heads 6. 84. 3-6; Bhīṣma strove to kill Pāñcālas while Arjuna fought with their adversaries to protect them 6. 89. 9; when Bhagadatta wanted to reach Yudhiṣṭhira, he had to fight a fierce battle with Pāñcālas who were prepared to fight with weapons (उद्यता-युधैः) 6. 91. 80; on the night of that day, Duryodhana reminded Bhīṣma of his vow to kill Pāñcālas 6. 93. 37; Bhīṣma assured Duryodhana that he would kill all Pāñcālas who were taking part in the war or would get himself killed by them 6. 94. 14-15; (44) On the ninth day, Duryodhana told Duḥśāsana that if they protected Bhīṣma, he would kill Pāñcālas who had made a common cause with Pāṇḍavas (यत्तान् पाञ्चालान् पाण्डवैः सह) 6. 101. 4; (45) On the tenth day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, protected by Pāñcālas, stood behind Sātyaki and Cekitāna in the Sarvaśatrunibarhaṇavyūha of Pāṇḍavas; Bhīṣma rushed towards them 6. 104. 4, 6, 29; Pāñcālas tried to check Bhīṣma who was killing his opponents 6. 105. 8; Bhīṣma dried up the lustre of the eminent and very strong Pāñcāla princes (पाञ्चालानां च ये श्रेष्ठा राजपुत्रा महाबलाः । तेषां आदत्त तेजांसि) 6. 105. 31; Bhīṣma sugge-sted to Yudhiṣṭhira, who was close to him, that if he desired Bhīṣma to be killed, Arjuna, Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas should jointly lead the attack on him; accor-dingly Arjuna, along with Pāñcālas and Cedis, and led by Śikhaṇḍin, marched towards Bhīṣma 6. 111. 15, 26; Bhīṣma in his battle with Matsyas and Pāñcālas, alone, killed innumerable elephants and horses, seven great chariot-fighters, and in addition five thousand chariot-fighters and fourteen thousand footsoldiers 6. 113. 21-22; when Bhīṣma killed seven great chariot-fighters, there arose a great roar (किलकिलाशब्दः) among Pāñcālas and others who, riding horses, chariots, ele-phants, and also those who fought on foot attacked Bhīṣma 6. 113. 46-48; when Bhīṣma fell, Pāñcālas blew conches 6. 114. 107; at his fall in the evening of the tenth day (सायाह्ने) Pāñcālas were delighted 6. 115. 7; (46) In the summary narration of the events which occurred while Droṇa was the general of the Kaurava army, it is mentioned that the large army of Pāñcālas was scattered by Droṇa when he agitated it and penetrated it (संक्षोभ्यमाणा द्रोणेन भिद्यमाना महाचमूः); they, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, trembled (समकम्-पन्त) while they got killed by Droṇa 7. 6. 34, 36; whenever Pāñcālas attacked Droṇa he killed them along with their horses and broke their chariots; ultimately Pāñcālas killed Droṇa by doing evil and cruel deeds (पाञ्चालैर् अशिवैः क्रूरकर्म-भिः । हतो रुक्मरथो राजन् कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् ॥ ) 7. 7. 20-21, 32; (47) On the eleventh day, Pāñcālas attacked the warriors led by Aśvatthāman who attacked Draupadī's sons 7. 15. 11; at the end of that day, they praised Arjuna when he declared the end of the war for the day 7. 15. 50; (48) On the twelfth day, Pāñcā-las attacked Droṇa; he scattered them away and repeatedly defeated them 7. 20. 18-19, 23; when a Pāñcāla prince (पाञ्चा-ल्य, not named) was killed by Droṇa, Pāñcālas attacked Droṇa shouting ‘kill Droṇa, kill Droṇa’; in the fierce battle, Droṇa threw the excessively angered Pāñ-cālas (भृशसंक्रुद्धान्) into disorder 7. 20. 46, 48-49; Pāñcālas, getting killed by Droṇa, trembled (समकम्पन्त) 7. 20. 53; they were broken (भग्न) by Droṇa 7. 21. 1; pierced by Droṇa's arrows, they were thrown back from their positions (चलितान्); Duryodhana pointed out to Karṇa Droṇa's feat and described the plight of Pāñcālas 7. 21. 7, 11-14; Pāñcālas gathered around Bhīma 7. 21. 23; of the twelve thousand great warriors of Pāñcālas six thousand followed Śikhaṇḍin 7. 22. 14; the remaining six thousand Prabha-drakas (Pāñcālas), riding chariots, with raised weapons and stretched bows, and making death as their common goal (समानमृत्यवो भूत्वा) followed Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna 7. 22. 36-37; Bhagadatta was en-circled by Yudhiṣṭhira and Pāñcālas; Bhaga-datta, riding his elephant, scattered them away; he forced them to run away 7. 25. 24, 26, 41; Pāñcālas, shouting ‘(attack) Droṇa’ (द्रोणम् द्रोणम् इति … पाञ्चालाः समचो-दयन्) incited one other; wherever Droṇa attacked the group of Pāñcāla chariot-fighters, Dhṛṣṭadyumna went to their help 7. 30. 6, 8; although afflicted by Droṇa's arrows (शरार्ताः), Pāñcālas did not give up fighting with him; Droṇa killed many of them 7. 31. 38-39; (49) On the thirteenth day, Pāñcālas, checked by Droṇa's arrows could not approach him who was protecting Kaurava army; that was a wonderful feat (तद् अद्भुतम् अपश्याम … । यद् एनं नाभ्यवर्तन्त पाञ्चालाः … ) 7. 34. 10; Bhīma assured Abhimanyu that he, Pāñcā-las and others would follow him when he entered the Cakravyūha 7. 34. 22; Duḥśā-sana told Duryodhana that he would kill Abhimanyu in the presence of Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas 7. 38. 22; when Duḥśāsana swooned in his encounter with Abhimanyu, Pāñcālas raised a loud roar; led by Yudhi-ṣṭhira they then attacked Droṇa's army 7. 39. 17-18; Pāñcālas and others attacked Jayadratha who foiled their attempt to follow Abhimanyu 7. 42. 18; Arjuna would have himself protected Abhimanyu if he had known that Pāñcālas could not do that 7. 50. 74; Subhadrā wondered who could kill Abhimanyu as though he was helpless when heroic Pāñcālas were there to help him 7. 55. 9; she felt contempt for the strength of Pāñcālas (पाञ्चालानां च धिग् बलम्) 7. 55. 12; (50) Saṃjaya told the grieving Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas would (at the end of the war) realize that the calamity was due to his fail-ure to adopt the right course (तत् ते बुद्धि-व्यभीचारम् उपलप्स्यन्ति … । पाञ्चाला … ) 7. 62. 7; (51) On the fourteenth day, Pāñcālas fought a fierce battle with Kurus in front of the व्यूह of Droṇa; Droṇa and many other kings on the side of Kauravas checked the onward march of Pāñcālas; when Kaurava army was being killed by Pāṇḍavas, Droṇa scattered away Pāñcālas with arrows 7. 70. 3, 13-14, 27; Pāñcāla chariot-fighters saved Dhṛṣṭadyumna from the attack of Droṇa 7. 72. 35; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya what did the Pāñcālas do when in their attempt to get close to Arjuna, they were checked by Droṇa (भारद्वाजेन संवृताः); Saṃjaya told him that in the afternoon of that day Kurus and Pāñcālas fought each other with Droṇa as the bet (अपराह्णे महाराज संग्रा-मे … । पाञ्चालानां कुरूणां च द्रोणे द्यूतम् अवर्तत ॥ ); Pāñcālas, wanting to kill Droṇa showered arrows on him; in the fierce battle, Pāñcālas, wanting to break the army, used important missiles (तदनीकं बिभित्सन्तो महास्त्राणि व्यदर्-शयन्) 7. 81. 1-5; demon Alambusa made a river of blood flow carrying away (dead) Pāñcālas 7. 83. 30; Droṇa killed twentyfive Pāñcāla warriors, known as great chariot-fighters and honoured by Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna (महारथसमाख्याता धृष्ट-द्युम्नस्य संमताः); he killed choice Pāñcāla warriors (पाञ्चालानां … वरान् वरान्) 7. 85. 28-29; when Droṇa defeated hundreds and thousands of Pāñcālas and killed many of them there went up a cry (of grief) (तेषाम् समभवच् छब्दो वध्य-तां द्रोणसायकैः) 7. 85. 31-32; gods, Gan-dharvas and others who were watching the battle pointed out to one another the runn-ing away Pāñcālas 7. 85. 33; in the absence of Sātyaki, Yudhiṣṭhira was to be prote-cted by Pāñcālas and others 7. 86. 45; Pāñcālas, when they faced Kṛtavarman, were attacked by him; hence they lost enthu-siasm (विगतोत्साहाः); but soon, like noble men, were ready to fight again desirous of attaining great fame (अतिष्ठन्न् आर्य-वद् वीराः प्रार्थयन्तो महद् यशः) 7. 88. 57-59 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 113. 67: आर्यवत् कुलीनवत् कुलीनत्वाद् इति यावत्); when defeated by Kṛtavarman they fled hither and thither 7. 90. 47-48; Dhṛtarāṣṭra wanted to know how Pāñcālas fought with Droṇa; both were deeply inimical to each other and Pāñcālas desired victory for Yudhi-ṣṭhira 7. 89. 41; Droṇa, having seen that his व्यूह was put into disorder by Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas, endeavoured to put it into order; he succeeded in pushing back Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas 7. 93. 35; brave Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍavas rushed from all sides on Droṇa to kill him 7. 97. 51; Duḥśā-sana had formed great enmity with Pāñcā-las 7. 98. 4; Droṇa hastened moderately to-wards Pāñcālas (जवम् आस्थाय मध्य-मम्) and put them to flight; announcing his name while fighting (नाम विश्राव्य संयुगे) he killed many of them 7. 98. 24-26; Pāñcālas covered Droṇa from all sides when he was checked by Vīraketu; they showered Droṇa with fiery arrows, costly Tomaras (तोमरैश् च महाधनैः) and various other weapons; Droṇa broke their arrows 7. 98. 30-32; Pāñcālas shouted that Droṇa would surrender to their king (वशम् एष्यति नो राज्ञः) 7. 98. 55; when the horses of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's chariot ran in all directions, Droṇa forced Pāñcālas to run away; defeating them Droṇa put his व्यूह in order (स्वं व्यूहं पुनर् आस्थाय) 7. 98. 57-58; when Duryodhana challenged Yudhiṣṭhira, Pāñcālas rushed towards him; Droṇa checked their advance 7. 100. 36-38; Dhṛṣṭaketu wanted to attack Droṇa who was killing Pāñcāla army 7. 101. 23; Pāñcālas trembled (समकम्-पन्त) as they were getting killed by Droṇa 7. 101. 47, 53; the great fighters of Pāñcālas were as though held at their thighs by Droṇa (ऊरुग्राहगृहीता हि पाञ्चालानां महारथाः) 7. 101. 49 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 125. 52: ऊरुग्राहः ऊरुस्तम्भः); when Cekitāna's charioteer was killed, Pāñcālas were afraid; Droṇa made them run away 7. 101. 67-68; when Pāñcāla army was reduced in number by Droṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira did not know who could go to save them 7. 102. 3-4; when the व्यूहस् of Pāṇḍavas were put into disorder, Pāñcālas and Pārthas went back a long way (व्यूहेष्व् आलोड्यमानेषु पाण्डवानां ततस् ततः । सुदूरम् अन्वयुः पार्थाः पाञ्चालाः सह सोमकैः ॥ ) 7. 102. 1; when Bhīma started to help Arjuna, Pāñcālas followed him 7. 102. 67: Droṇa wanted to remain at his place to check the advancing Pāñcālas 7. 105. 21; Dhṛtarāṣṭra told Saṃjaya that if ever Pāñcālas were to fight with Bhīma they would not be able to protect their lives (न भीममुखसंप्राप्तो मुच्येतेति मतिर् मम । … न पाञ्चाला … जानन्ति युधि संरब्धा जीवितं परिरक्षितुम्) 7. 110. 22-23; Duryodhana pointed out to Droṇa, Śikhaṇḍin who led the Pāñcāla army 7. 125. 11; he told Droṇa that either he would kill Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍa-vas or else get killed by them 7. 125. 25; Droṇa felt himself sinking in the sin of Dhṛṣṭadyumna since he had not yet killed him, Śikhaṇḍin and Pāñcālas (मज्जन्तम् इव चात्मानं धृष्टद्युम्नस्य किल्बिषे); he could not take off his armour until he had killed Pāñcālas 7. 126. 25, 32; (52) In the fierce battle that was fought during the night between fourteenth and fifteenth day the reporters on the battlefield like Saṃjaya could distinguish the Pāñcālas from Kurus only by hearing their personal names and the names of their respective गोत्रस् and families (गोत्रानां नामधेयानां कुलानां चैव तुआरिष । श्रवणाद् धि विजानीमः पाञ्चालान् कुरुभिः सह ॥ ); Pāñcālas fled in all directions when they were being killed by Duryodhana 7. 128. 2, 8, 17; at that time Pāñcālas led by Bhīma attacked Duryodhana; when deeply wounded, Duryodhana sat down in his chariot, Pāñcālas felt he was dead and delightfully they raised a loud cry 7. 128. 21, 23; when Duryodhana attacked Yudhi-ṣṭhira, Pāñcālas advanced towards him; Droṇa faced them 7. 128. 33; Drupada, protected by Pāñcālas turned towards Droṇa; six thousand Pāñcālas, led by Śikha-ṇḍin, rushed towards Droṇa 7. 129. 8, 10; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya when Droṇa, after the death of Jayadratha and Bhūriśra-vas, attacked Pāñcālas, what did Arjuna do ? when Droṇa entered the Pāñcāla army, how was he (later) killed ? 7. 130. 3, 7; when Droṇa used Vāyavyāstra, Pāñcālas ran away due to fear; but when Bhīma and Arjuna invaded the Kaurava army, Pāñcālas followed them 7. 132. 38, 41; Karṇa asked Duryodhana to save the Kaurava warriors attacked on all sides by Pāñcālas and others; Pāñcāla chariot-fighters, feeling victorious and delighted, were making loud sound; he assured Duryodhana that he would kill Pāñcālas who had come forward to fight 7. 133. 3, 4, 6, 11; the victorious Pāñcālas raised a cry seeing Karṇa engaged in battle with Pāṇḍavas; Duryodhana asked his army to stand still for he was going to kill the atta-cking Pāñcālas; he also requested Aśva-tthāman to kill Pāñcālas since they, feeling victorious, moved in the Kaurava army like forest-fire; Aśvatthāman was born for killing Pāñcālas and make the world devoid of them; that was declared by the Siddhas, and it was bound to be true (करिष्यसि जगत् सर्वम् अपाञ्चालं किलाच्युत । एवं सिद्धाब्रुवन् वाचो भविष्यति च तत् तथा । ); Pāñcālas would not be able to withstand the अस्त्रस् of Aśvatthāman 7. 134. 11, 54, 76-77, 79-81; Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana that he would fight with Pāñcālas for Duryodhana's delight; they would run away in all directions when burnt down by his arrows; when Yudhiṣṭhira would see Pāñcālas dead, he would be dejected; Aśvatthāman then challenged Pāñ-cālas to steady themselves and fight with him; he asked their great chariot-fighters to strike him showing their skill in the use of अस्त्रस् (प्रहरध्वम् इतः सर्वे मम गात्रे महारथाः । स्थिरीभूताश् च युध्य-ध्वं दर्शयन्तो ऽस्त्रलाघवम् ॥ ); when addressed, Pāñcālas showered weapons (arrows ?) on Aśvatthāman (शस्त्रवृष्टिम् अपातयन्); Aśvatthāman repulsed the arrows and killed ten heroes in the presence of Pāṇḍavas and Dhṛṣtadyumna; when Pāñcālas were getting killed, they ran away in all directions; seeing that, Dhṛṣṭadyumna rushed at Aśvatthāman; in the duel that ensued, Dhṛṣṭadyumna was covered on all sides by the entire Pāñcāla army; Aśvatthāman, by his well-joined arrows, forced hundreds and thousands of Pāñcālas to flee (बाणैः संनतपर्व-भिः); he killed a hundred Pāñcālas with a hundred arrows (शतेन च शतं हत्वा), and three great chariot-fighters with three sharp arrows (त्रिभिश् च निशितैर् बाणैर् हत्वा त्रीन् वै महारथान्); he thus killed a large number of those Pāñcālas who were prepared for fight (नाशयाम् आस पाञ्चालान् भूयिष्ठं ये व्यवस्थिताः); Pāñcālas, thus getting killed, left Aśvatthā-man and went away with their chariots and banners shattered; Aśvatthāman having defeated his enemies, uttered a loud roar 7. 135. 10, 11, 13; 16-21; 36, 47, 49-52; Droṇa used वायव्यास्त्र against Pāñcālas; getting killed, they ran away; when Bhīma and Arjuna attacked the left and the right flank respectively (बीभत्सुर् दक्षिणं पार्श्वम् उत्तरं तु वृकोदरः), great chariot-fighters among Pāñcālas followed them; Droṇa blew away (व्यधमत्) the Pāṇḍava army and Pāñcālas at the start of the night (रजनीमुखे) 7. 136. 11, 14; 7. 137. 51; Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya, when Droṇa entered the Pāñcāla army and burnt their hosts of chariots who prote-cted him on all the four sides 7. 139. 12-14; when Pāñcālas and Kauravas killed one another they raised a fierce sound (आसीन् निष्टानको घोरो निघ्नताम् इतरेतरम्) 7. 139. 32; Yudhiṣṭhira asked Pāñcālas and others to attack Droṇa to kill him; then, raising fearful cries they attacked him 7. 140. 2-3; when Aśvatthāman swooned while fighting with Ghaṭotkaca, Pāñcālas raised a loud roar 7. 141. 32; when Duryo-dhana, while fighting with Bhīma, lost his charioteer and horses, he was considered dead; Pāñcālas then attacked Droṇa 7. 141. 60; after defeating Sahadeva, Karṇa turned towards Pāñcālas 7. 142. 16; when Śikha-ṇḍin was defeated by Kṛpa. Pāñcālas covered him on all sides 7. 144. 27; they also covered him when he attacked Droṇa 7. 145. 3; in the great battle that followed between the two heroes, Pāñcālas also took part 7. 145. 68; when Sātyaki and Duryodhana were engaged in battle, there was confused and fierce fighting between Bhāratas and Pāñcālas (ततः समभवद् युद्धम् आकुलम् … । पाञ्चालानां च सर्वे-षां भारतानां च दारुणम् ॥ ) 7. 146. 17; incited by Duryodhana, Droṇa fought fiercely and started killing Pāñcālas; then they raised a tumultuous cry; when they were broken and shattered, dejected Kṛṣṇa pointed out to Arjuna their plight 7. 147. 15, 22-23; he advised Arjuna to assist their great chariot-fighters, as well as Bhīma, to give encouragement to the entire army (आश्वासनार्थं सर्वेषां सैन्यानाम्) 7. 147. 29; Karṇa oppressed the great chariot-fighters among Pāñcālas (पाञ्चालानां महारथान् । अभ्यपीडयत्); pressed hard by Karṇa, the large Pāñcāla army ran away (सा पीड्यमाना तु कर्णेन पाञ्चालानां महाचमूः । संप्राद्रवत् सुसंत्रस्ता); their warriors fell down from horses, ele-phants and chariots; Karṇa cut off their hands, heads and thighs; Droṇa assisted him 7. 148. 9-19; Kṛṣṇa pointed out to Ghaṭotkaca their plight 7. 148. 45; Pāñcālas, smiling, watched the battle between Karṇa and Ghaṭotkaca 7. 152. 5; Pāñcālas, oppressed excessively by Alāyudha, had no peace of mind (न शान्तिं लेभिरे तत्र … भृशपीडिताः) 7. 152. 31; Karṇa forced the Pāñcāla महारथस् to run away; then they fought with Droṇa; they raised a loud roar when Alāyudha was killed by Ghaṭotkaca 7. 153. 8, 10, 33; Karṇa attack-ed Pāñcālas led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin 7. 154. 3-4; Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that every night Duryodhana asked Karṇa to kill next day Arjuna (or Kṛṣṇa) with his शक्ति so that the Pāñ-cālas could be ruled as if they were servants (प्रेष्यवत् पाण्डुपाञ्चालान् उप-भोक्ष्यामहे ततः)—Pāñcālas who were like the leaves of a tree in the form of the Pāṇḍavas (पाञ्चालाः पत्रसंज्ञिताः) 7. 157. 19-22; Dhṛtarāṣṭra was curious to know how the Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas who, armed and in battle-arrays (व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः) fought with Droṇa when they attacked him (7. 158. 13); when, Yudhi-ṣṭhira after the death of Ghaṭotkaca started to fight with Kauravas, Pāñcālas armed for battle (दंशिताः) beat भेरिस् and blew conches 7. 158. 50; Droṇa vowed that he would take off his armour only after he had killed Pāñcālas 7. 160. 12; towards the end of the night war, Droṇa divided his army into two parts and, led by Duryodhana, attacked Pāñcālas;
