they were specifically afflicted by the arrows of Droṇa; yet, although suffering from excessive pain, Pāñcālas continued to fight (पाञ्चालास् तु विशेषेण द्रोणसायक-पीडिताः । समसज्जन्त राजेन्द्र समरे भृशवेदनाः) 7. 161. 3, 28; when Droṇa killed Virāṭa, Drupada, and other warriors of Pāñcālas, Dhṛṣṭadyumna cursed the Pāñcāla warriors who would let Droṇa remain alive or turn away from him; Pāñcālas then attacked Droṇa, but they could not even look at Droṇa although they tried, protected as he was by Duryo-dhana and others (यतमानापि पाञ्चाला न शेकुः परिवीक्षितुम्) 7. 161. 35-37, 38, 40; (53) On the fifteenth day, when the large armies of Kauravas and Pāñcālas clashed with one another, everything was in turmoil and nothing was quite clear (आविग्नम् अभवत् सर्वम् … न प्राज्ञायत किंचन); in the raised dust it was difficult to know who were Kaura-veyas and who Pāñcālas 7. 162. 22, 27-28; during the duel between Karṇa and Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira addressed the chief heroes of Pāñcālas and urged them to go and help the chief warriors of Pāṇḍavas (पाञ्चालानां नरव्याघ्रान् … तत्र गच्छत यत्रैते युध्यन्ते मामका रथाः); Pāñcālas, thus urged, divided their army into four parts (चतुर्धा वाहिनीं कृत्वा): a part hit Droṇa with arrows; others, led by Bhīma, covered him from another side (पाञ्चा-लास् त्व् एकतो द्रोणम् अभ्यघ्नन् बहुभिः शरैः । भीमसेनपुरोगाश् च एकतः पर्य-वारयन् ॥ ); Arjuna was urged to separate Kurus from Droṇa; then Pāñcālas would kill Droṇa whose protectors were slain; but Droṇa attacked Pāñcālas and killed them; however, they continued to attack Droṇa; as they were getting killed a fearful sound was raised by them; when Pāñcālas were thus getting killed, Pāṇḍavas were afraid and they lost hope of victory (वध्य-मानेषु संग्रामे पाञ्चालेषु॥।पाण्डवान् भयम् आविशत् । … नाशंसुर् विजयं तदा ॥ ) 7. 164. 48-54, 56-58, 60-63; after the false news of Aśvatthāman's death twenty thousand Pāñcāla principal heroes (नर-र्षभाः) showered arrows from all sides on Droṇa; he then used ब्रह्मास्त्र to kill Pāñcālas; with that missile he cut off their heads and large arms adorned with gold ornaments (तथैव परिघाकारान् बाहून् कनकभूषणान्) and killed twenty thou-sand Pāñcāla chariot-fighters (विंशति-साहस्रान् पाञ्चालानां रथव्रजान्) 7. 164. 78-83; that day Kauravas, led by Droṇa, had started fighting only with Pāñcālas (पाञ्चालैर् एव केवलैः), and when Droṇa released the ब्रह्मास्त्र, especially Pāñcālas were killed (पाञ्चालाश् च विशेषतः । … व्यन-शन्); when their armies were thus thrashed, Pāñcālas, (though) angered, turned away from battle (अमर्षवशम् आपन्नाः पाञ्चाला विमुखाभवन्) 7. 165. 98, 100-101, 104; Droṇa killed hosts of chariot-fighters of Pāñcālas but was killed 8. 4. 5; (54) After the death of Droṇa, Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana that he would try to kill Pāñcālas by all sorts of means, whether soft or harsh (सर्वोपायाइर् … कर्मणा येन तेनेह मृदुना दारुणेन वा); only after killing Pāñcālas he would have peace of mind; he would force Pāñcālas to run away by the use of Nārāyaṇāstra 7. 166. 28-29, 52; Sahadeva, in order to pacify Sātyaki, told him that the Pāṇḍavas had no allies other than Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis and Pāñcālas; similarly the Pāñcālas had no allies other than Pāṇḍavas and Vṛṣṇis 7. 169. 48, 50; when, after the death of Droṇa, Kauravas and Pāṇḍava-Pāñcālas became ready to fight, Aśvatthāman aimed his Nārāyaṇāstra against the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas; Yudhiṣṭhira, afraid of the effects produced by the अस्त्र, asked Dhṛṣṭadyu-mna to run away with Pāñcāla army; he also remembered that Pāñcālas. led by Satyajit and making effort for his victory, were totally destroyed by Droṇa (पाञ्चालाः सत्यजिन्मुखाः । कुर्वाणा मज्जये यत्नं समूला विनिपातिताः) 7. 170. 10, 15, 26, 34; Duryodhana urged Aśvatthāman to use Nārāyaṇāstra again when Pāficālas, wishing victory, had steadied themselves (व्यवस्थिता हि पाञ्चालाः पुनर् एव जयैषिणः); Aśva-tthāman told him his inability to do that but he forced Pāñcālas to run away wound-ing them with arrows; when Aśvatthāman succeeded in killing many prominent (Pāñcāla) heroes on the side of Pāṇḍavas he blew his large conch with delight; hearing that all Pāñcālas, and even Bhīma, ran in all directions leaving Dhṛṣṭadyumna behind 7. 171. 25, 45, 67; (55) Saṃjaya, summarizing the events between the death of Droṇa and that of Karṇa, told Dhṛta-rāṣṭra that Duryodhana assured his army that they would be witnesses to the heroism of Karṇa and Aśvatthāman against the Pāñcālas; Karṇa killed and afflicted many Pāñcālas, but was ultimately killed by Arjuna 8. 2. 15, 18, 20; 8. 5. 30; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra remembered that Karṇa had once be-fore defeated Pāñcālas and made them pay tribute (अजैषीत् … पाञ्चालांश् च … चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 18-20 (reference to Karṇa's conquests before the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice of Duryodhana 3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. I. 24. 28-34); (56) On the sixteenth day, Duryodhana requested Karṇa to lead the Kaurava army because when Pāñcālas would see him they would run away; Pāṇḍavas together with Pāñcālas would be disheartened on seeing Karṇa ready to fight (पाण्डवा गतचेतसः … पाञ्चालैः सह); the bards urged Karṇa to kill Pāñcālas and bring victory to Kauravas; they also said that Pāñcālas would not be able to withstand Karṇa ready with his arms 8. 6. 30-31, 40, 42; Pāñcālas and others rushed at the Kaurava army; their chariot-fighters, elephant-riders and impor-tant foot-soldiers, delighted, danced and laughed making different sounds (नाना-विधरवैर् हृष्टा नृत्यन्ति च हसन्ति च) 8. 8. 19-20; Karṇa put to death twenty Pāñcāla chariot-fighters along with their horses and charioteers and felled down their banners; he also killed many other Pāñcālas; then Pāñcāla princes (? पाञ्चाल-पुत्राश् च) attacked Karṇa 8. 16. 16, 22-23; heroes from the east and south, skilled in elephant-warfare, showered arrows, तोमरस् and नाराचस् on Pāñcālas; Pāñcā-las, with sharp weapons, surrounded the elephants and showered arrows on them; they covered Nakula to protect him from those who were fighting from elephants; Karṇa, after defeating Nakula, turned towards Pāñcālas; Pāṇḍavas raised a loud cry seeing Karṇa approach Pāñcāla chariot-fighters (दृष्ट्वा सेनापतिं यान्तं पाञ्चालानां रथव्रजान् 8. 17. 99); their chariots then were carried away (by horses) with or without the charioteers and their axles broken; those Pāñcāla महा-रथस् who survived began to run away; Karṇa, showering arrows, persecuted Pāñ-cālas whose armours and banners were broken and tormented them with arrows 8. 17. 7, 21, 98-99, 101, 119-120; those Pāñcālas who survived the war of eighteen days followed Pāṇḍavas to the lake (पाञ्-चालानां च ये शिष्टाः) 9. 29. 21, 46, 52: Duryodhana even in that condition wished to destroy the enthusiasm of Pāñcālas 9. 30. 43; Pāñcālas and other Pāṇḍava warriors clapped each other's palms (अन्योन्यस्य तलान् ददुः); Duryo-dhana considered that to be his insult; angered, he said that he would send Pāṇḍa-vas and Pāñcālas to the abode of Yama 9. 31. 13, 30, 40-44; when Duryodhana fell down, Pāñcālas, delighted (प्रहृष्ट-मनसः), threw up their upper garments and made roaring sounds; some expressed their joy by stretching their bows, others by sounding bow-strings; some blew big conches and still others beat दुन्दुभिस्; some made sportive gestures and laughed (चिक्रीडुश् च तथैवान्ये जहर्षुश् च); they said many things in praise of Bhīmasena 9. 60. 3-16; hearing that, Kṛṣṇa rebuked them 9. 60. 17-18; hearing Kṛṣṇa's words reassuring Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas for the means they adopted to defeat Kauravas, Pāñcālas were very much delighted; they roared like herds of lions (भृशसंहृष्टा विनेदुः सिंहसंघवत्); Aśvatthāman assured Duryodhana that he would kill all Pāñcālas with all sorts of means in the very presence of Kṛṣṇa (सर्वोपायैर् हि नेष्यामि प्रेतराजनिवेशनम्) 9. 64. 35; (a reference to this incident in 1. 2. 180); (62) References to what happened during the night of the eighteenth day are found at the beginning of the Śalyaparvan: (i) Vaiśaṃpāyana told Janamejaya that during that night the three heroes on the side of Kauravas who survived the war (हतशिष्टास् त्रयो रथाः) killed the entire Pāñcāla army; that was told by Saṃjaya to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra 9. 1. 13, 30; (ii) Dhṛtarāṣṭra remem-bered that Duryodhana had assured him that he would kill all Pāñcālas; he then asked Saṃjaya to tell him how all Pāñcā-las, together with foot-soldiers, were killed (पाञ्चालाश् च यथा सर्वे निहताः सपदा-नुगाः) 9. 2. 22, 63; (63) In the night of the eighteenth day Aśvatthāman re-solved to kill Pāñcālas when they were asleep; he told Kṛpa that Pāñcālas, tired due to exertion, would sleep that night delightfully, trustfully, feeling themselves victorious, unyoking their horses and keep-ing away their armours; he would storm Pāñcālas in their camp to kill them with his sword and then get peace of mind; he would repay the debt he owed to his father by killing Pāñcālas; by killing the Pāñcāla army at night he will have done his duty and feel happy 10. 1. 53; 10. 3. 25, 28-32, 34-35; earlier when Bhīma had stepped on Duryodhana's head, Pāñcālas growled, laughed, blew conches and sounded दुन्दुभिस् 10. 1. 58-59; Kṛpa told Aśva-tthāman that they should kill Pāñcālas next day in battle; but Aśvatthā-man asked Kṛpa why he did not blame Pāñcālas who had committed sin by not following धर्म and broken all norms of life (एवम् अधार्मिकाः पापाः पाञ्चाला भिन्नसेतवः); he had therefore decided to kill them during their sleep 10. 5. 24-25; (65) When Pāñcāla and Kuru women saw their husbands and relatives lying dead on the battlefield they fell down from their chariots; tired and helpless they were almost deprived of their consciousness (श्रान्तानां चाप्य् अनाथानां नासीत् काचन चेतना) 11. 16. 13-15; पारतक: Pārataka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Mleccha people of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … ) 6. 10. 63, 5; these म्लेच्छ tribes are described as cruel (दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः । … हूणाः पारतकैः सह) 6. 10. 64.
पारद: Pārada m. (pl.): Name of a people characterized as म्लेच्छस्। A. Location: They are mentioned along with other north-western tribes like Daradas, Dārvas, Bāhlīkas and others (वायव्या दरदा दार्वाः … पारदाः बाह्लि-कैः सह) 2. 48. 12; (शकाः … यव-नाः पारदास् तथा) 7. 97. 13; 7. 68. 41; however, they are said to have been born in the bay (?) of the ocean and around Sindhu river (समुद्रनिष्कुटे जाताः परिसिन्धु च मानवाः । ते … पारदाश् च) 2. 47. 9-10 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11 takes निष्कुट to mean a house-garden: समुद्रसमीपस्थनिष्कुटे गृहो-द्याने … ). B. Characteristic: They main-tained themselves on grains which grew of their own accord or on those cultivated with river water (इन्द्रकृष्टैर् वर्तयन्ति धान्यैर् नदीमुखैश् च ये) 2. 47. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11: इन्द्रकृष्टैः इन्द्रे-णैवाकृष्टैः न तु कर्षणादिक्षेत्रिययत्ना-पेक्षैः वनधान्यैः वृष्ट्यभावे तु नदी-मुखैः नदीप्रभवैः). C. Descrip-tion: Very frightful and having terrible eyes; they knew the tricks of Asuras (विदन्त्य् असुरमायां ये सुघोरा घोर-चक्षुषः) 7. 68. 41. D. Epic events: (1) They brought for the Rājasūya of Yudhi-ṣṭhira tribute of different kinds like goats and sheep (अजाविकम्), cows, donkeys, camels, gold, and jewels, wine made from fruits (फलजं मधु) and blankets (कम्बलान्), but were stopped at the gate (द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 10-11; their kings (राजन्याः, क्षत्रियाः) brought wealth by hundreds for the Rājasūya 2. 48. 12, 16, (13); (2) On the eighth day of war they accompanied Droṇa who marched out immediately after Bhīṣma 6. 83. 7; (3) On the fourteenth day, a large number of them were killed by Arjuna 7. 68. 41, (33, 37, 44); on the same day, they, along with Śakas and others and led by Duryo-dhana, attacked Sātyaki; there were three thousand horse-riders of them (त्रीणि सादि-सहस्राणि) 7. 97. 13; they were killed by Sātyaki 7. 97. 20.
पारसीक: Pārasīka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध … ) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तिलकाः पारसीकाश् च) 6. 10. 51.
पार्वतीय: Pārvatīya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people living in mountainous regions; their kings are also referred to as Pārvatīyas. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (ससैरन्ध्राः पार्वतीयाश् च) 6. 10. 56. B. Description: Living on mountains (शैलवासिन्) 7. 97. 32; heroic (शूर) 3. 255. 8; 5. 30. 24; 7. 97. 15, 26, 29, 37-38; wrathful, fond of wars, strong, firm-fisted (संरम्भिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दृब्धपाणयः) 8. 51. 19; very strong (सुमहाबल) 2. 48. 6; difficult to be defeated (दुर्जय) and difficult to look at (दुर्दर्श) 8. 31. 13; (great) chariot-fighters (रथ) 5. 196. 6; 7. 97. 15; (महारथ) 3. 255. 8; rough like mountains (विषमा यथैव गिरयस् तथा) 8. 30. 79; they fought with rocks and were expert in fighting with rocks (पाषाणयोधिन्, अश्म-युद्धेषु कुशलाः) 7. 97. 15, 29-30; 34-35, 37-38; not cruel (अनृशंस) and of good character and conduct (शीलवृत्तोपपन्न) 5. 30. 24; they could not be defeated by any one except Arjuna (न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप) 8. 51. 20. C. Epic events: (1) Pārvatīyas brought for the Rajasūya tribute in the form of black chowries and other chow-ries white like moon, ample sweet honey gathered from Himalayan flowers; flowers brought down by waters from Uttara Kurus, and powerful herbs from northern Kailāsa; they were stopped at the gate and not allowed to enter (कृष्णाल् लला-मांश् चमराञ् शुक्लांश् चान्याञ् शशिप्र-भान् । हिमवत्पुष्पजं चैव स्वादु क्षौ-द्रं तथा बहु ॥ उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यस् चाप्य् अपोढं माल्यम् अम्बुभिः । उत्तराद् अपि कैलासाद् ओषधीः सुमहाबलाः ॥ … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 48. 5-7; (2) Arjuna killed five hundred Pārvatīya chariot fighters who accompanied Jaya-dratha 3. 255. 8; (3) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to convey to all the Pārva-tīya kings who had sided with Duryo-dhana against Pāṇḍavas that he enquired about their welfare (तेषां सर्वेषां कुशलं तात पृच्छेः) 5. 30. 23-24; (4) Pārvatīya chariot-fighters, along with others, marched towards Kurukṣetra in the second division of the army (द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 6, 8, 11; (5) On the twelfth day of war, Pārvatīyas and others formed the back (पृष्ठ) of the Suparṇavyūha of the Kauravas 7. 19. 4, 11; (6) On the fourteenth day, five hundred chariot-fighters of Pārvatīyas attacked Sātyaki; they were all expert in fighting with rocks; hence Duḥśāsana in-cited them to attack Sātyaki who was not expert in fighting with rocks: Sātyaki cut off with नाराच arrows their arms and killed, first, five hundred and then many thousands of them 7. 97. 15, 29-38; (7) On the seventeenth day, Pārvatīyas, led by Śakuni, and Ulūka, guarded the extreme end (प्रपक्ष) of the right wing (दक्षिणम् पक्षम्) of the व्यूह of the Kauravas 8. 31. 11-13; Kṛṣṇa listed Pārvatīyas among those who took the side of the Kurus for the sake of Duryodhana and who could not be defeated by any body except Arjuna 8. 51. 19-20; (8) Saṃjaya listed Pārvatī-yas among those who were killed in the war (पार्वतीयाश् च यवनाश् च निपातिताः) 9. 1. 26; (9) Vasudeva listed Pārvatīya kings (पार्वतीयांस् तथा नृपान्) among those who were formerly defeated by Kṛṣṇa 16. 7. 11; earlier Dhṛtarāṣṭra also had referred to the same event 7. 10. 16. D. 1. Some persons referred to as पार्व-तीय: (i) Janamejaya (a certain king who was killed by Durmukha) 8. 4. 70; (ii) Śakuni 2. 56. 10; 3. 35. 3; 5. 30. 27; 2. Their excellent horses are also referred to as Pārvatīya (पार्वतीयान् … हयवरान्) 7. 97. 26.
पालन: Pālana nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. It is the fourth in a cluster of seven Varṣas of the Kuśadvīpa which is situa-ted to the north of Jambhudvīpa (उत्तरेषु च … द्वीपेषु) 6. 13. 1; (चतुर्थं पालनं स्मृतम् । … सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्जकाः) 6. 12. 12-13; for the description of the people which is common to all the Varṣas of the Kuśadvīpa (6. 13. 14-15) see Audbhida.
पिशाच: Piśāca m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Called Janapada (पिशाचा दरदाश् चैव … एते जनपदा राजन्) 6. 46. 49-50. B. Epic events: (1) On the second day of war, Piśācas on the side of the Pāṇḍavas, along with Daradas, Puṇḍras and others, stood on the right side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39, Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 49-50. (2) On the eighth day, led by Bhagadatta, Piśācas on the side of Kauravas marched behind Droṇa 6. 83. 8; (3) On the fourteenth day, led by Duryodhana, they attacked Sātyaki who was trying to reach Arjuna 7. 97. 14; (4) Listed among those who were defeated by Kṛṣṇa 7. 10. 16. C. Their relationship with Bāhlīkas: According to a certain Brāhmaṇa who was speaking in the Kuru assembly Bāhlīkas were the progeny of two Piśācakas called Bahi and Hlīka who lived near Vipāśā and they were not created by Prajāpati (बहिश् च नाम ह्लीकश् च विपा-शायां पिशाचकौ । तयोर् अपत्यं बाह्लीका नैषा सृष्टिः प्रजापतेः ॥ ) 8. 30. 44. D. A female reciter of an अनुवंश श्लोक: A certain Piśāca woman (पिशाची), wear-ing mortar-like ear-ornaments, used to recite अनुवंश श्लोकस् near the gate of Kurukṣetra (अत्रानुवंशं पठतः शृणु मे कुरुनन्दन । उलूखलैर् आभरणैः पिशाची यद् अभाषत ॥ … द्वारम् एतद् धि कौन्तेय कुरुक्षेत्रस्य … ) 3. 129. 8, 11 (the औन्वंश श्लोकस् are 3. 129. 9-10) (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 8: अनुवंशं परंपरागतम् आख्यानश्लोकम्).
पुण्ड्र: Puṇḍra(ka) m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; the people, warriors and their certain kings also desi-gnated as Pauṇḍra(ka); once used as an adj. (2. 13. 19). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5: (पुण्ड्रा भार्गाः किराताश् च) 6. 10. 49; (ओष्ट्राः पुण्ड्राः ससैरन्ध्राः) 6. 10. 56; located along the eastern ocean: From Magadha, Arjuna directed the Aśvamedha horse to the south along the sea passing through Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras and Keralas (पाण्डवः  … दक्षिणां दिशम् आस्थाय चारयाम् आस तं हयम् 14. 84. 1; ततः समु-द्रतीरेण वङ्गान् पुण्ड्रान् सकेरलान्) 14. 83. 29; called Janapada also in 6. 46. 49-50 (पुण्ड्राः … एते जनपदा राजन्). B. Origin: Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, created Puṇḍras from her foam (पुण्ड्रान्  … फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह) 1. 165. 36. C. Social status: Paunḍras, listed among those Kṣatriyas who became degraded as वृषल because they disregarded Brāhmaṇas (पौण्ड्राः … क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 17-18; and also because they violated the धर्म of Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियाः केचित् … तेषां … प्रजा वृषलतां प्राप्ता ब्राह्मणा-नाम् अदर्शनात् ॥ त एते … पुण्ड्राश् च … । वृषलत्वं परिगता व्युत्थानात् क्षत्रधर्-मतः । ) 14. 29. 14-16; called म्लेच्छस् (पुण्ड्रान् सकेरलान् । तत्र तत्र च भू-रीणि म्लेच्छसैन्यान्य् अनेकशः विजिग्ये॥। धनंजयः) 14. 83. 29-30. D. Special feature: Their warriors fought riding ele-phants; they were skilled in fighting battles while riding elephants (गजयोधिनः; गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3. E. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍu spread the fame of Kurus in the Puṇḍra country (पुण्ड्रेषु … कुरूणाम् अकरोद् यशः) 1. 105. 12; (2) King Vāsudeva was known as ‘Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva’ among the Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras and Kirātas (वङ्ग-पुण्ड्रकिरातेषु राजा … । पौण्ड्रको वासु-देवेति … लोकेषु विश्रुतः) 2. 13. 19; Bhīma, in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya, defeated the king of the Pauṇḍra people in battle (पौण्ड्राधिपं  … वासुदेवम् … निर्जित्याजौ) 2. 27. 20-21; (3) Puṇḍra Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds for the Rājasūya (आहार्षुः क्ष-त्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 15-16; they (Puṇḍrakas) also brought fine cloth, silk and woolen materials, and mantles; they were asked by the gatekeepers to bring more; when they brought additional tribute they were allowed to enter through the gate (for citation see Tāmralipta) 2. 48. 17-20; a Pauṇḍra king (not named, Vāsudeva ?), among others, served as server at Rāja-sūya (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् … सपौ-ण्ड्रोड्रान् … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 22; (4) On the second day of war, Puṇḍras were one of the Janapadas who stood at the right wing (दक्षिणं पक्षम्) of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of Pāṇḍavas 6. 46. 49-50; (5) On the third day, Puṇḍras (पुण्ड्राविषस् तथा ?) stood at the left wing (वामं पक्षम्) of the Gāruḍa-vyūha (6. 52. 2) of Kauravas 6. 52. 9; (6) Among the past exploits of Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentioned his victory over Puṇḍras in battle 7. 10. 15; (7) On the the twelfth day, Pauṇḍras formed the back of the Suparṇavyūha (पृष्ठे … पौण्ड्र-मद्रकाः) (7. 19. 4) of Kauravas 7. 19. 11; (8) On the fourteenth day, Arjuna killed Puṇḍras and others in hundreds and thousands (न ते स्म शक्याः संख्यातुम् व्राता शतसहस्रशः) 7. 68. 42-43; (9) On the sixteenth day, Karṇa's former victory over Puṇḍras mentioned by Dhṛta-rāṣṭra 8. 5. 19 (a reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before Duryodhana's Vaiṣṇava-yāga 3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. I. 24. 28-34); the same day, incited by Duryodhana, Puṇḍras, riding elephants, attacked Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna showering him with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराच arrows 8. 17. 2; (10) Arjuna, accompanying the horse for the Aśvamedha, reached Puṇḍras in the south and conquered their म्लेच्छ armies (म्ले-च्छसैन्यान्य् अनेकशः) 14. 83. 30. F. Certain kings called Puṇḍra, Puṇḍraka, king of the Pauṇḍras or they have the epithet पौण्ड्रक: (1) Puṇḍra 1. 1. 174; Puṇḍraka 2. 4. 21; (2) A king (Vāsu-deva ?): पौण्ड्राधिप 2. 27. 20; he was known among Puṇḍras, Aṅgas and Kīrātas as Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva 2. 13. 19.
पुरुषादक: Puruṣādaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. They brought for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira large quantities of gold and silver as tribute but were stopped at the gate (पुरुषादकान् ॥ … द्वारि वारितान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्यं रज-तं बहु) 2. 47. 15-16.
पुलिन्द: Pulinda m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (पुलिन्दाः कल्कलैः सह) 6. 10. 60; listed among those who were natives of Dakṣiṇāpatha (दक्षिणापथजन्मानः … उत्साः पुलिन्दाः) 12. 200. 39; their capital town Pulinda-nagara was in the south (ततो दक्षिणम् आगम्य पुलिन्दनगरं महत्) 2. 26. 10. B. Description: Cruel (क्रूर), rough while fighting (संग्रामकर्कश) 8. 15. 10; wrathful (संरम्भिन्), fond of fighting (युद्धशौण्ड), strong (बलिन्), firm-fisted (दृब्धपाणि) 8. 51. 19; they could not be defeated by any one except Arjuna (न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुम् त्वदन्येन परं-तप) 8. 51. 20; sinful, they lived like dogs, crows, बलस् (?), and vultures (एते पाप-कृतो … श्वकाकबलगृध्राणाम् सधर्-माणो) 12. 200. 41; in the Kaliyuga (3. 186. 27), their sinful kings, given to lying, ruled the wrong way (मिथ्यानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः) 3. 186. 29, 30. C. Social status: Classed as म्लेच्छस् 3. 186. 29; they lived in countries but led the life of दस्युस् (विषयवासिनः … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 14-15; they did not exist in the Kṛtayuga but were to be found since the Tretāyuga; they are listed among those who did not believe in Bhūtapati being the अध्यक्ष (of the world) (एष भूतपतिस् तात स्वध्य-क्षश् च प्रकीर्तितः । निरध्यक्षांस् तु कौन्तेय कीर्तयिष्यामि तान् अपि ॥ उत्साः पुलिन्दाः) 12. 200. 38-39; नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रेताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते) 12. 200. 42; they were originally Kṣatriyas, but became degraded to the status of a वृषल due to disregarding Brā-hmaṇas (पुलिन्दाश् … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजात-यः ॥ वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 33. 20-21; those who do not offer sacrifices do not obtain heaven and remain established in the lower worlds like Pulindas and Śabaras (अर्वाक् च प्रति-तिष्ठन्ति पुलिन्दशबरा इव । न ह्य् अयज्ञा अमुं लोकं प्राप्नुवन्ति कथंचन । ) 12. 147. 8. D. Epic events: (1) Bhīma in his expedition before the Rājasūya went to east (2. 23. 4; 2. 26. 1, 7, 9) and then to the South to reach the capital town of Pulindas; he vanquished there Sukumāra and Sumitra, the kings of Pulindas (ततो दक्षिणम् आगम्य पुलिन्दनगरं महत् । सुकुमारं वशे चक्रे सुमित्रं च नरा-धिपम् ॥ ) 2. 26. 10; (2) Pulindas formed a part of Duryodhana's army 5. 158. 20; 8. 51. 20; (3) On the eighth day of war, they followed Droṇa who was behind Bhīṣma standing in the forefront of the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas 6. 83. 7, 22; (4) On the sixteenth day, Pāṇḍya king killed Pulindas riding horses and fighting with शक्ति, प्रास, and arrows (सशक्तिप्रास-तूणीरान् अश्वारोहान्) depriving them of their weapons and arrows with his arrows 8. 15. 9-10. E. Past event: Māndhātṛ asked Indra the nature of the धर्म to be followed by people like Pulindas and how they should be made to behave properly by kings like him (कथं धर्मं चरे-युस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः) 12. 65. 14-15; Indra then taught the धर्म of Dasyus 12. 65. 17-23. [See Pulindaka].
पुलिन्दक: Pulindaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed separately from Pulinda by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhārata-varṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सिन्धुपुलिन्दकाः) 6. 10. 39. [See Pulinda].
पौरक: Pauraka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their kings (राजन्याः 2. 48. 13; क्षत्रि-याः 2. 48. 16) brought tribute in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (पौरका … । … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजात-शत्रवे) 2. 48. 13, 16.
पौरव: Paurava (Pauravaka) m. (pl.): Name of a people, and general characterization of those born in the family cf Pūru; only once referred to as Pauravaka (6. 46. 47). A. Origin: The lineage of Pūru known as Paurava (पूरोस् तु पौरवो वंशः) 1. 80. 27; (पूरोः पौरवाः) 1. 90. 10; (त्वं मे वंशकरः सुतः । पौरवो वंश इति ते ख्यातिं लोके गमिष्यति) 1. 70. 45. B. Characteristics of their kings: of famous conduct and wise (प्रथितवृत्त, विज्ञानशालिन्); no one of them ever lacked character, heroism or progeny (न ह्य् अस्मिञ् शीलहीनो वा निर्वीर्यो वा … प्रजाविरहितो वापि भूतपूर्वः कदाचन ॥ ) 1. 89. 2-3; they were heroic, and in lustre they equalled Indra (वीराञ् शक्रप्रतिमतेजसः) 1. 89. 4; their acts did not distress others (अक्लिष्टकर्-मन्) 1. 109. 20; the poem narrating the Paurava dynasty was in every respect holy, brought good fortune, wealth, long life and fame (वंशं पौरवाणां च सर्वशः ॥  … पुण्यं स्वस्त्ययनं महत् । धन्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यं) 1. 70. 2; their warriors were great archers (महेष्वास) 7. 145. 46. C. Epic events: (1) Śaṃtanu anointed his son Bhīṣma as the crown prince of Pauravas (पौरवेषु ततः पुत्रं यौवराज्ये ऽभ्यषेचयत्) 1. 94. 38; Bhīṣma gratified the Pauravas by his conduct (पौरवाञ् … रञ्जयाम् आस वृत्तेन) 1. 94. 39; (2) On the second day of war, Yudhiṣṭhira, with Pauravakas and others formed the back (पृष्ठम्) of the Krauñ-cāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39, Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 46. 47; (3) On the third day, Dhṛṣṭaketu, along with Paura-vas and others stood at the right tip (दक्षिणं शृङ्गम् आस्थाय) of the Ardha-candravyūha (6. 52. 10) of Pāṇḍavas 6. 52. 13; (4) On the fourteenth day, Sātyaki said that Pauravas (on the side of the Kauravas) and others were no match for Arjuna (कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्) 7. 86. 28-29; (5) Hearing the sound of the chariot and of Gāṇḍīva (श्रूत्वा तु रथनिर्-घोषं गाण्डीवस्य च निस्वनम्), Karṇa guessed that Arjuna had killed Śibis and Pauravas (on the side of the Kaura-vas) 7. 145. 45-46. D. Past events: Śakuntalā chose as a boon from Kaṇva that those born in the lineage of Pūru be firm in the practice of धर्म and not lose their kingdom (ततो धर्मिष्ठतां वव्रे राज्याच् चास्खलनं तथा । … पौरवाणाम्) 1. 67. 33. E. Various persons called as descendants of Pūru, delighters of Pūru's descendants, propagators or bearers of the line of Pūru: (A) Descendant of Pūru: (i) पौरव: (1) Duḥṣanta 1. 68. 59; 1. 69. 32, 34; (2) Śaṃtanu 1. 94. 38; (3) Saṃvaraṇa 1. 89. 39; (ii) पौरवदायाद: Son of Viḍūratha (not named) 12. 49. 67; (iii) पौरवाणां … वंशे जातः: Pāṇḍu 1. 109. 20; (B) Those who carry further the line of Pauravas: (i) पौरवाणां वंशकरः: Duḥṣanta 1. 62. 3; (ii) पौर-वं वंशम् उद्वहन्: Taṃsu, son of Matināra 1. 89. 12; (iii) पूरोर् वंश-करान् नृपान् many kings 1. 89. 1; (iv) पूरोर् वंशधरान् (नृपान्) 1. 89. 4: (C) Delighter of the Pauravas: पौरवनन्दन (1) Bharata 1. 89. 19; (2) Vasu Upari-cara 1. 57. 2; (iii) Śaṃtanu 1. 93. 16; (iv) Saṃvaraṇa 1. 160. 14.
प्रकुत्सक: Prakutsaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मधुमन्तः प्रकुत्सकाः) 6. 10. 51.
प्रचेत: Praceta m. (pl.): Name of a people. Bṛhadbala, the king of Pracetas, listed by Bhīma among the sixteen kings who extirpated their kinsmen, friends and rela-tives (ये समुच्चिछिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् … प्रचेतानां बृहद्बलः) 5. 72. 11, 16.
प्रतिमत्स्य: Pratimatsya m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (दुगूलाः प्रतिमत्स्याश् च) 6. 10. 50.
प्रतीच्य: Pratīcya m. (pl.): General chara-cterization of the western people; once mentioned as Janapada (6. 114. 77). A. Description of their warriors: Brave (शूर) 8. 4. 49 and skilled in using all kinds of weapons and missiles (सर्व-शस्त्रास्त्रकुशल) 6. 16. 17; while fighting they put on ornaments, besides armour and good garments (सवर्माम्बरभू-षण) 8. 4. 49; they were all brought up in noble families (कुले ये च विवर्धिताः) 8. 4. 49. B. Epic events: (1) To en-courage Duryodhana, Karṇa reminded him that kings of the west, along with the rest, were made to pay tributes to him ( … प्रतीच्योदीच्यवासिनः । कृताः करप्रदाः सर्वे राजानस् ते नराधिप) 3. 226. 3; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to convey to western and other kings who had joined the side of Duryodhana that he wished them well (प्राच्योदीच्या … तेषां सर्वेषां कुशलम् तात पृच्छेः) 5. 30. 23-24; (3) Duryodhana's army was guarded among others by the kings of the west 5. 158. 19-20; their chariot-fighters mentioned among those who marched towards Kurukṣetra in Duryodhana's second division (दाक्षि-णात्याः प्रातीच्याश् च … एते महारथाः सर्वे द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 6, 8; (4) Before the start of the war, Duryo-dhana instructed Duḥśāsana that the main concern of westerners and others should be to protect Bhīṣma 6. 16. 17; (5) On the ninth day, Pratīcyas, though they were getting killed by sharp arrows, did not abandon Bhīṣma when he was fighting with Pāṇḍava heroes (प्रतीच्योदीच्यमा-लवाः । … संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः) 6. 102. 7; (6) On the tenth day, Pratīcyas were among the twelve Janapadas who, though they were pierced by arrows and wounded, did not leave Bhīṣma alone who fought with Arjuna (द्वादशैते जनपदाः शरार्ता व्रणपी डिताः । संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं युध्यमानं किरीटिना ॥ ) 6. 114. 76-77; (7) On the eleventh day, Pratīcyas and others, led by Duryodhana, were behind Karṇa who marched in front of all archers (प्रतीच्योदीच्यवासिनः । … तवात्मजं पुरस्कृत्य सूतपुत्रस्य पृष्ठतः ॥ ययौ वैकर्तनः कर्णः प्रमुखे सर्वधन्वि-नाम् 7. 6. 6-8; तावकानां मुखं कर्णः 7. 6. 21) of the Śakaṭavyūha of the Kaura-vas 7. 6. 15; (8) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna, while boasting himself before Yudhiṣṭhira said that it was he who had killed Pratīcyas and others 8. 49. 96; (9) mentioned by Saṃjaya among those who were killed in battle by Arjuna in the first seventeen days of war 8. 4. 47; (10) Saṃ-jaya, while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, men-tioned Pratīcyas among those all of whom were killed (उदीच्या निहताः सर्वे प्रतीच्याश् च नराधिप) 9. 1. 27.
प्रदर: Pradara m. (pl.): Name of a people. They lived in the region between the mountains Meru and Mandara along the river Śailodā and enjoyed the pleasing shade of the bamboos and reeds; their kings (नृपाः) brought Pipīlaka variety of gold, given as boon by ants, in heaps to be measured by द्रोण as tribute for the Rājasūya; they also brought much other tribute but were stopped at the gate 2. 48. 2-7; (for details and citations see Ekāśanājyoha).
प्रभद्रक: Prabhadraka m. (pl.): Name of a section of Pāñcālas; they figure only in the context of war where they were led generally by Śikhaṇḍin or Dhṛṣṭadyumna. A. Description: Very quick (in action) (शीघ्रतर), expert (in fighting) (विशा-रद), whose strength was like that of a lion (सिंहसमानवीर्य) 5. 47. 30; heroic while fighting battles (पृतनाशूर) 6. 19. 21; very difficult to be conquered (सुदुर्-जय) 10. 8. 47; cruel (क्रूर) 7. 70. 45; six thousand of Prabhadrakas (here speci-fically said to be Pāñcālas (प्रभद्रकास् तु पाञ्चालाः) with ready weapons rode chariots that were drawn by excellent horses of different colours and were adorned with variegated banners having gold shafts; they stood with stretched bows and shook their enemies by discharging arrows; they were always determined to die together (उदायु-धाः । नानावर्णैर् हयश्रेष्ठैर् हेम-चित्ररथध्वजाः ॥ शरव्रातैर् विधुन्वन्-तः शत्रून् विततकार्मुकाः । समानमृत्यवो भूत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नं समन्वयुः ॥ ) 7. 22. 36-37. B. Epic events: (1) Arjuna told Saṃjaya that in war when Prabha-drakas would strike down the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Duryodhana would repent (प्रभद्रका॥।यदा क्षेप्तारो धार्त-राष्ट्रान्) 5. 47. 30; (2) Mentioned among those who were on the side of Yudhiṣṭhira (पाञ्चालास् च प्रभद्रकाः) 5. 56. 33; as part of the army of the Pāṇḍa-vas, they marched towards Kurukṣetra 5. 149. 50; they with Nakula, Sahadeva and others and led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna (धृष्टद्युम्नमुखान्) were ordered by Yudhiṣṭhira to set out first towards Kuru-kṣetra 5. 197. 12; (3) On the first day of war, in the Vajravyūha of Pāṇḍavas (6. 19. 7), Prabhadrakas, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, were among those who guarded the rear (पृष्ठगोपाः) of Bhīma 6. 19. 20-21; on that day Bhīṣma killed Prabhadrakas and others (पाञ्चालान् … प्रभद्रकान्) 6. 45. 54; (4) On the third day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, along with Pāñcālas and Pra-bhadrakas stood in the middle of the Ardhacandravyūha (6. 52. 10) of Pāṇḍa-vas (पाञ्चालाश् च प्रभद्रकाः) 6. 52. 14; (5) On the tenth day, Prabhadrakas trem-bled (समकम्पन्त) when they heard the rattle produced by Droṇa's chariot 6. 107. 48; (6) On the thirteenth day, all Prabhadrakas were among those who were to follow Abhimanyu after he penetrated the Cakravyūha (पाञ्चालाः … सर्वे प्र-भद्रकाः) 7. 34. 22; (7) On the four-teenth day, an Āvantya (not named) check-ed the march of Dhṛṣṭadyumna who was helped by Prabhadrakas 7. 70. 45; in the evening of that day, six thousand striking Prabhadrakas and Pāñcālas, led by Śhikha-ṇḍin, attacked Droṇa (प्रभद्रकाश् च पाञ्चालाः षट्सहस्राः प्रहारिणः) 7. 129. 10; (8) During the night war, Śikhaṇḍin with three thousand Prabhadrakas followed Yudhiṣṭhira when he started to fight with Karṇa (त्रिसाहस्रैः प्रभद्रकैः) 7. 158. 49; Yudhiṣṭhīra wanted Prabhadrakas and others to attack Droṇa 7. 159. 5; (9) On the sixteenth day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍin and Prabhadrakas attacked the army of Kauravas 8. 8. 14; on the same day Pāṇḍava heroes, aided by Prabhadra-kas, fought with the army of elephants attacking them; the elephants crushed them with feet and broke them with tusks; but Prabhadrakas and their leaders continued to shower arrows on elephants 8. 17. 7-10, 26; they were among those excellent warriors (प्रवीराः) who oppressed Karṇa (सर्वे कर्णम् अपीडयन्) 8. 21. 25; (10) On the seventeenth day Karṇa killed seventyseven excellent Prabhadraka warriors (प्रभद्र-काणां प्रवरान् अहनत् सप्तसप्ततिम्); ex-cellent (प्रवीराः) Prabhadrakas attacked Karṇa 8. 32. 32, 42; they checked the advance of Karṇa (Vasuṣeṇa) in the direction of Yudhiṣṭhira 8. 33. 21; when Karṇa, angered, rushed towards Yudhi-ṣṭhira many Prabhadrakas and other Pāṇḍava heroes attacked him from diffe-rent sides (विचेरुः) 8. 40. 66; Prabhadra-kas and other Pāṇḍava heroes attacked the army of Kauravas 8. 44. 7; Prabhadra-kas attacking Karṇa appeared like entering the mouth of a big fish or falling in the wide open mouth of Death (महाझष-स्येव मुखं प्रपन्नाः; … मृत्योर् आस्यं व्यात्तम् इवान्वपद्यन् प्रभद्रकाः) 8. 47. 10; (11) On the eighteenth day, Śalya, after he became the general of the Kaurava army, boasted that all Prabhadrakas, Pāñcālas and the rest would see his valour (पाञ्चालाश् चैव … सर्वे चापि प्रभद्र-काः ॥ विक्रमं मम पश्यन्तु) 9. 6. 13-14; he killed Prabhadrakas by his arrows 9. 10. 21; Śikhaṇḍin, aided by Prabhadra-kas, engaged Kṛtavarman and Kṛpa (Gautama) in battle 9. 14. 7; after the death of Śalya, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, along with Prabhadrakas, attacked the elephants encir-cling them 9. 24. 35; Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the Prabhadrakas killed the army of Duryo-dhana 9. 26. 6; (12) During the night of the eighteenth day, Prabhadrakas were awakened by the loud sound; they and Śikhaṇḍin afflicted Aśvatthāman by dis-charging arrows (शिली मुखैः … द्रोण-पुत्रं समार्दयन्); seeing them shower-ing arrows (शरवर्षाणि वर्षतः), he uttered a loud roar wishing to kill them 10. 8. 46-47; Prabhadrakas and Śikhaṇḍin attacked him with all sorts of weapons (नानाप्रहरणैर्); Aśvatthāman first kill-ed them all with sword 10. 8. 59, 61, 63; (13) On the nineteenth day, in the fore-noon (पूर्वाह्णसमये 9. 1. 14), Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra that all Prabha-drakas were killed in war 9. 1. 29 [See Pāñcāla].
प्रमुद: Pramuda m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुदोष्णाः प्रमुदास् तथा) 6. 10. 49.
प्रवाह: Pravāha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबो-ध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वानरास्याः प्रवाहाश् च) 6. 10. 43.
प्राच्य: Prācya m. (pl.): General designation of the eastern people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas of Bhārata-varṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरत-र्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (द्रविडाः केरलाः प्राच्या … ) 6. 10. 57; also mentioned while listing the twelve Janapadas (द्वादशैते जनपदाः) 6. 114. 77. B. Description: Expert in the use of all kinds of weapons and missiles (सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रकुशल) 6. 16. 17; excellent fighters (प्रवीर) and expert in fighting while riding elephants (गजयो-धिन्) 8. 17. 2; (गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 3; (मातङ्गयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 12. 102. 4; Prācyas employed deceitful means while fighting (शठयोधिन्) 12. 102. 4. C. Social status: According to Karṇa, Prācyas were Dāsas (प्राच्या दासा … ) 8. 30. 73. D. Epic events: (1) Yudhi-ṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to inform the Prācya and other kings who had joined Kauravas that he enquired about their welfare (कुश-लं तात पृच्छेः) 5. 30. 23-24; (2) Accord-ing to Saṃjaya, in the war, Prācyas would be killed by Bhīma (प्राच्याश् च … भीम-सेनस्य भागतः) 5. 56. 14; (3) Duryo-dhana's royal army (राजचमू) included Prācyas 5. 158. 19-20; a part of them were to form the second division while marching out of Hāstinapura to Kuru-kṣetra (द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 7-8; (4) In war, Prācyas and others were assigned the duty of protecting Bhīṣma 6. 16. 14, 17; (5) On the second day of war, Bhīṣma, protected by Prācyas, Sauvīras and others, suddenly rushed towards Arjuna 6. 48. 21; (6) On the third day, at the instance of Bhīṣma, Prācyas, Sauvīras and others rushed towards Arjuna; they were killed by him, that was his great feat, unequalled by others (महत् कृतम् कर्म धनंजयेन कर्तुं यथा नार्हति कश्चिद् अन्यः) 6. 55. 74, 130; (7) On the ninth day, Sauvīras, Prācyas and others did not aban-don Bhīṣma although they were struck by sharp arrows (वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः) 6. 102. 7; (8) On the tenth day, instigated by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102-106), Prācyas and others attacked Arjuna as moths jump on fire (पतङ्गा इव पावकम्) 6. 112. 109-110; a little while before the fall of Bhīṣma, when others ran away, Prācyas were among the twelve Janapadas who, though pierced by arrows and afflicted due to wounds (शरार्ता व्रणपीदिताः), did not leave Bhīṣma alone 6. 114. 76-77; (9) On the eleventh day, they followed Karṇa who marched out at the head of all archers (प्रमुखे सर्वधन्विनाम्) 7. 6. 8; (10) On the twelfth day, Prācyas were stationed at the ‘neck’ (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Suparṇavyūha of Kauravas 7. 19. 4, 7-8; (11) On the fourteenth day, at the instance of Duryodhana, Prācyas and others, riding huge elephants (कुञ्जरैः पर्वतोपमैः), attacked Arjuna; he cut off their heads and arms adorned with ornaments 7. 68. 32-33; (12) On the sixteenth day, Saṃjaya mentioned Prācyas among those who, during the first fifteen days of war were killed by Arjuna 8. 4. 47; on that day, as ordered by Duryodhana, excellent Prācya warriors, riding elephants, attacked Pāñcālas and showered them with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराचस् (शर-तोमरनाराचैर् वृष्टिमन्त इवाम्बुदाः) 8. 17. 1-4; (13) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna, while boasting in the presence of Yudhiṣṭhira, said that it was he who had destroyed Prācyas (प्राच्या निरस्ता … ) 8. 49. 96; (14) On the eighteenth day, Kṛṣṇa, while praising Bhīma for his deeds, mentioned that he had killed Prācyas in the great war (महायुद्धे निहताः) 9. 32. 22; (15) In the forenoon (पूर्वाह्णसमये 9. 1. 14) of the nineteenth day, Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra that all Prācyas were killed in war 9. 1. 27; (16) Vasudeva told Arjuna that Kṛṣṇa had once defeated Prācyas 16. 7. 11.
प्रावर: Prāvara(ka) m. (sg.): Name of a Deśa. One of the Deśas on the Krauñcadvīpa (देशांस् तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि); Prāvaraka lay beyond the Deśa called Uṣṇa, and beyond Prāvara was the Deśa called Andhakāraka (उष्णात् परः प्रावरकः प्रावराद् अन्धकारकः) 6. 13. 20-21; (Was Prāvaraka also related to the mountain Vāmana ? 6. 13. 20); all these Deśas were visited by gods and Gandharvas (एते देशा महाराज देवगन्धर्वसेविताः) 6. 13. 23.
प्रावृषेय: Prāvṛṣeya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; मह्युत्तराः प्रावृषेया … ) 6. 10. 49.
प्राहूत: Prāhūta m. (pl): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सुदेष्णाः प्राहूतास् … ) 6. 10. 45.
प्रोष्ठ: Proṣṭha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जन-पदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (केकरकाः प्रोष्ठाः) 6. 10. 60.
परशुवन: Paraśuvana nt.: Name of a hell. The name literally means ‘forest of axes’; it is described as ‘a great hell’ (परमनिरय, महानिरय) 12. 309. 30-31; a doer of evil deeds, who is covetous, to whom untruth is dear, who is always engaged in deception, he, due to these cheatings (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 321. 31: उपनिधिभिश् छलेन), goes to this hell and experiences great unhappiness; he plunges into the great river Vaitaraṇī whose waters are hot and then gets his limbs cut by the leaves of trees which are sharp like a sword; ultimately he falls in-to the Paraśuvana hell; he lives there experiencing great affliction (यो लुब्धः सुभृशं प्रियानृतश् च मनुष्यः सतत-निकृतिवञ्चनारतिः स्यात् । उपनिधिभिर् असुखकृत् स परमनिरयगो भृशम् असुखम् अनुभवति दुष्कृतकर्मा ॥ उष्णां वैतरणीं महानदीं अवगाढो ऽसिपत्र-वनभिन्नगात्रः । परशुवनशयो निपतितो वसति च महानिरये भृशार्तः ॥ ) 12. 309. 30-31.
परावह: Parāvaha m.: Name of the last of the seven winds. A. Divine origin: All the seven winds are Aditi's sons ( … एते ऽदितेह् पुत्रा मारुताः) 12. 315. 53. B. Description: The highest (पर) and difficult to transgress (दुरति-क्रम) 12. 315. 52; very wonderful (पर-माद्भुत) 12. 315. 53; blowing constantly without break in all places and sustaining all (creatures) (अनारमन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः) 12. 315. 53. C. Activity: It blows in the seventh of the seven paths of winds which blow on the earth and in the atmosphere (पृथिव्याम् अन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः) 12. 315. 31 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 31: संवान्ति संगच्छन्ति); it takes away the lives of living beings at the time of their death; both Mṛtyu (Death) and Vaiva-svata (Yama) follow its path; it leads those to immortality who, with their intellect calm and steady in आत्मन्, understand (the world) correctly and who take delight in the practice of meditation; having met Parā-vaha ten thousand sons of Dakṣa Prajāpati reached quickly the end of directions; one who is created (touched ?) by it, is de-feated; he goes away never to return (?) (सर्वप्राणभृतां प्राणान् यो ऽन्तकाले निरस्यति । यस्य वर्त्मानुवर्तेते मृत्यु-वैवस्वताव् उभौ ॥ सम्यग् अन्वीक्षतां बुद्ध्या शान्तयाध्यात्मनित्यया । ध्याना-भ्यासाभिरा माणाम् यो ऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ यं समासाद्य वेगेन दिशाम् अन्तं प्र-पेदिरे । दक्षस्य दश पुत्राणां सहस्राणि प्रजापतेः ॥ येन सृष्टः (स्पृष्टः ?) परा-भूतो यात्य् एव न निवर्तते । परावहो नाम परो वायुः स दुरतिक्रमः ॥ 12. 315 49-52 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 49-52; मृत्युवैवस्वताव् अपि यदनुरेधिनौ तयोर् अपि प्रेरक इत्य् अर्थः । एतेन मृत्यु-ग्रस्तानां ब्रह्मादीनां तदधीनत्वं कैमुतिकन्यायसिद्धं ॥ ४९ । ।भो अध्या-त्मचिन्तकाः … शान्तया बाह्याभ्यन्तर-विषयेभ्य उपरतया बुद्ध्या सम्यग् अहं ब्रह्मास्मीति वाक्यानुसन्धानपूर्व-कं अन्वीक्षतां श्रवणमननम् अनु-ध्यानेन पश्यतां ध्यानाभ्यासो निरन्-तरं ध्यानम् एव अभिरामं येषां तेषां यो ऽमृतत्वाय मोक्षाय कल्पते ॥ ५० । । दिशो ऽन्तं प्रतिपेदिरे ब्रह्माण्डं निर्-भिद्य गता इत्य् अर्थः ॥ ५१ । ।).
परिवह: Parivaha m.: Name of the sixth of the seven winds. A. Divine origin: All the seven winds are Aditi's son's ( … ऽदितेः पुत्रा मारुताः) 12. 315. 53. B. Description: Very wonderful (परमाद्भुत) 12. 315. 53; very speedy (जवतां वरः) 12. 315. 48. C. Activity: (a) Common to all seven winds: They all blow incessantly in all direction and sustain all (creatures) (अनारमन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्व-धारिणः) 12. 315. 53 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 31: संवान्ति संगच्छन्ति); they blow along the seven paths of winds which blow together on the earth and in the atmosphere (पृथिव्याम् अन्त-रिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः । सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै) 12. 315. 31; (b) Special to Parivaha: Due to its circular movement the heavenly waters flow in the atmosphere (and do not fall down); it supports the holy waters of celestial Gaṅgā; being checked by this wind from a distance the sun, though he is the source of a thousand rays and brightens up the earth, appears like having a single ray; due to this wind the moon, which is the heavenly store of nectar, waxes (after waning) (यस्मिन् पारिप्लवे दिव्या वहन्त्य् आपो विहायसा । पुण्यं चाकाशगङ्गायास् तोयं विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ॥ दूरात् प्रतिहतो यस्मिन्न् एकरश्मिर् दिवाकरः । योनिर् अंशुसहस्रस्य येन भाति वसुन्धरा ॥ यस्माद् आप्यायते सोमो निधिर् दिव्यो ऽमृतस्य च । षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स वायुर् … ) 12. 315. 46-48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 46: परितः उपर्य् एव यस्य वेगात् पतन्ति न त्व् अधः पतन्तीति परिप्लवः । स्वार्थे तद्धितः॑यः तोयं विष्टभ्य आकाशे एवावस्थाप्य).
पारिजात: Pārijāta m.: Name of one of the five heavenly trees. Past event: Vidura scolds Duryodhana, who wanted to arrest Kṛṣṇa, by reminding him that Kṛṣṇa had defeated even Indra when he took away the Pārijāta tree from him (पारिजातं च हरता जितः साक्षाच् छचीपतिः) 5. 128. 48; Dhṛtarāṣṭra while describing the best exploits of Kṛṣṇa men-tions that he had frightened Amarāvatī and removed the Pārijāta from the abode of Indra ( … त्रासयित्वामरावतीम् । म्छेन्द्र-भवनाद् वीरः पारिजातम् उपानयत्) 7. 10. 22. (Its use in pl. in 3. 220. 23 (पारिजात-वनैः) and 9. 36. 60 (पारिजातैः) denotes the coral trees in general and hence those references do not belong here).
पुष्पक: Puṣpaka nt.: Name of a विमान (a vehicle moving in the air). A. Origin: It was fashioned by Viśva-karman (विश्वकर्मणा । विहितम्) 3. 158. 35. B. Description: Moving in the air (खेचर) 3. 275. 52: drawn by swans (हंसयुक्त) 9. 46. 27; moving at will (कामग) 3. 275. 52; heavenly (दिव्य) 9. 46. 27; brilliant (श्रीमन्त्) 3. 158. 35; (विराजन्त्) 3. 275. 52; pleasant (रुचिर) 3. 221. 5; (मनोरम) 9. 46. 27; equipped with excellent beds and seats (शय्यासन-वर) 3. 158. 35; having variegated borders (चित्रपर्यन्त) 3. 158. 35. C. Epic event: After Bhīma's fight with the Yakṣas, when the Pāṇḍavas came to meet Kubera, he was seated in the Puṣpaka 3. 158. 35. D. Rāmā-yaṇa events: (1) When Rāvaṇa defeated Kubera and drove him out of Laṅkā, he deprived Kubera of his Puṣpaka Vimāna; Vaiśravaṇa, however, cursed Rāvaṇa that the Vimāna would never carry him; it would carry only him who would kill Rāvaṇa in a battle (न त्वाम् एतद् वहिष्यति । यस् तु त्वां समरे हन्ता तम् एवैतद् वहिष्यति) 3. 259. 34-35; (2) Rāma, after making arrange-ments for the internal security of Laṅkā (विधाय रक्षां लङ्कायां) crossed the ocean riding the Puṣpaka 3. 275. 51-52; (3) Rāma reached Kiṣkindhā riding the Puṣpaka; on way he described to Sītā the forest from the Vimāna (वैदेह्या दर्शयन् वनम्) 3. 275. 56; (4) When Rāma was anointed the king of Ayodhyā, he wor-shipped the Puṣpaka and returned it to Vaiśravaṇa (पुष्पकं च विमानं तत् पूज-यित्वा) 3. 275. 68. E. Mythological events: (1) When Skanda was anointed the leader of the army of the gods (यदाभिषिक्तो  … सेनापत्येन पावकिः), Śiva started to meet him at Bhadravaṭa; at that time Kubera, riding his Puṣpaka, was in front of Śiva 3. 221. 1, 5; (2) Kubera practised austerities near a तीर्थ, which came to be known as Kauberatīrtha; as a result, Kubera received various boons and, as a gift, the Puṣpaka Vimāna as his vehicle (वाहनं चास्य तद् दत्तं … विमानं पुष्पकं) 9. 46. 27.
प्रतिस्मृति: Pratismṛti (f.): Name of a science. A. Description: Called a science (विद्या), a perfection in bodily form (सिद्धिं मूर्तिमतीं) 3. 37. 27; a secret knowledge (उपनिषद्) 3. 38. 9; (ब्रह्मन्) 3. 37. 36; 3. 38. 10; excellent योगविद्या (योगविद्याम् अनुत्तमाम्) 3. 37. 34. B. Its power: When Arjuna would learn it, he would be able to propitiate Rudra, Mahendra, Varuṇa, Kubera and Dharmarāja (Yama) to obtain their weapons 3. 37. 27-28; when one knows that science, the whole world dawns on him (जगत् सर्वं प्रकाशते) 3. 38. 9. C. Epic event: It was taught by Vyāsa to Yudhiṣṭhira when he was ready to receive it and was sanctified (प्रपन्नाय शुचये) 3. 37. 34-35, 27; Yudhiṣṭhira memorized it by reciting it from time to time (मनसा … धारयाम् आस … काले काले समभ्यसन्) 3. 37. 36; he later taught it to Arjuna who was initiated by him (दीक्षित) to receive it 3. 38. 13-14; it was taught to him in a secluded and private place (विविक्ते, रहसि) 3. 38. 2-3, 9, 14; when endowed with Pratismṛti science, Arjuna was to practise austerities and wait for the proper time to receive the favour of the gods (तेन त्वं ब्रह्मणा तात संयुक्तः … । देवतानां यथाकालं प्रसादं प्रतिपालय) 3. 38. 10.
प्रवह: Pravaha m.: Name of the first of the seven winds. A. Divine origin: All the seven winds are Aditi's sons ( … अदितेः पुत्रा मारुताः) 12. 315. 53 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 53: अदितेः खण्डनशून्याया अदीनायाः परम-चितेः पुत्रा इव पुत्रा रूपभेदाः). B. Description: (a) Common to all winds: All the seven winds are very wonderful; they blow incessantly in all directions sus-taining all (creatures) (परमाद्भुताः । अनारमन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्व-धारिणः ॥ ) 12. 315. 53; (b) Peculiar to Pravaha: Subtle (सूक्ष्म), cool (शीत), fragrant (सुगन्धिन्), pleasant to touch (सुखस्पर्श); most mysterious (पर-माद्भुत) 12. 315. 53; the best among the seven winds; it blows to auspicious worlds (सप्तानां मरुतां श्रेष्ठो लोकान् गच्छति यः शुभान्) 12. 290. 72. C. Activity: They all move along the seven paths of winds which blow on the earth and in the atmosphere (पृथिव्याम् अन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः । सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै … ) 12. 315. 31; this particular Pravaha wind, which impels the clouds which arise due to smoke and heat, blows on the first of the seven paths of the winds (प्रेरयत्य् अभ्रसंघातान् धूमजांश् चोष्मजांश् च यः । प्रथमः प्रथमे मार्गे प्रवहो नाम सो ऽनिलः) 12. 315. 36; the perfected ascetics (मुनयः सिद्धा … ), after death, are first borne by the rays of the sun (तान् … सूर्यो वहति रश्मिभिः); there, the Pravaha wind receives them and carries them further to the highest point of नभस्; (ultimately they reach Nārāyaṇa and do not return to this world) (स तान् वहति … नभसः परमां गतिम्) 12. 290. 69-72, (74-75); those who are versed in the Sāṃkhya philosophy know the (character of) the Pravaha wind which is one of the seven winds 12. 290. 27.
